articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Aston Villa y al Arsenal en Villa Park este lunes
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Aston Villa y al Arsenal en Villa Park este lunes
articles.body: El Aston Villa recibe al Arsenal este lunes en Villa Park en el primer gran examen liguero de la temporada para ambos conjuntos, que hasta ahora solo han disputado un partido de Premier League. El cuadro de Unai Emery viene de una situación delicada tras un verano de salidas importantes. Cayó goleado por 4-0 en su visita al Brighton, en un partido que se decidió en apenas 31 minutos de la primera mitad, con una desafortunada acción defensiva que propició el primer gol y un doblete de Jack Hinshelwood que sentenció el resultado antes del descanso. Favorito para el partido entre Aston Villa y Arsenal El Arsenal, por su parte, empezó su defensa del título de la manera más solvente posible. Se impuso 3-0 al recién ascendido Coventry City en el Emirates, con goles de Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka y Martin Ødegaard, en un partido que resolvió con autoridad y sin apenas sobresaltos. Con un Villa que llega tocado tras su severa derrota y un Arsenal que confirmó sus credenciales de candidato, el favoritismo visitante es claro para las casas de apuestas. 1XBET paga la victoria del Arsenal a cuota 1.54, por 4.16 del empate y 6.1 del triunfo del Aston Villa. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan se apoya en el único partido de Liga que han disputado hasta ahora ambos conjuntos. El Aston Villa no fue capaz de marcar ante el Brighton, dejando su casillero goleador a cero en su estreno, mientras que el Arsenal, además de anotar tres goles ante el Coventry, no encajó ninguno, mostrando una solidez defensiva notable en las primeras semanas de temporada. Con estos antecedentes, la probabilidad en las apuestas deportivas de que ambos equipos vean puerta este lunes se reduce considerablemente. 1XBET paga el no a 1.87, por 1.85 del caso contrario. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles también encuentra referencias claras en el estreno de ambos equipos. El duelo del Villa en Brighton dejó cuatro goles en el marcador, mientras que el del Arsenal ante el Coventry se cerró con tres. Sumando ambos antecedentes y la superioridad ofensiva que ha mostrado el conjunto de Mikel Arteta, el mercado se inclina por un partido con goles en el marcador. 1XBET sitúa la cuota del +2.5 goles totales a 1.81, por 2 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners también se apoya en el primer y único partido de Liga disputado por ambos conjuntos. El Arsenal generó un buen número de ocasiones y de saques de esquina ante el Coventry, favorecido por su dominio absoluto del balón durante los 90 minutos, un patrón que suele repetirse cuando el equipo de Arteta se enfrenta a rivales que se ven obligados a replegarse. El Aston Villa, por su parte, apenas inquietó la portería rival en Brighton, lo que también se tradujo en una escasa generación de córners propios durante ese partido.

articles.title: 76ers news: Jaylen Brown shares moment with viral fan
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown said an official goodbye to Boston as he heads to Philadelphia to fulfill his NBA duties for the 76ers. But before making his final address to t...
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown said an official goodbye to Boston as he heads to Philadelphia to fulfill his NBA duties for the 76ers. But before making his final address to the Celtics fans, the star forward met his passionate 6-year-old fan, Gio .

In a post shared by Courtside Buzz, Brown could be seen holding Gio in his arms, while this time around, the young fan was in the 76ers colors. When the video first went viral, Gio was wearing a Boston jersey, pleading with the former Celtics superstar to return to the city.

Earlier last month, a video on Instagram went viral in which Gio was seen crying passionately when his mother asked him why he was sad and whether he would still love his favorite NBA player after moving to a different city.

"I love you so much. You mean a lot to me, and you are my favorite player in the whole NBA. And thank you for everything that you did with the Celtics," Gio was heard saying in the video.

The Instagram video had close to 10 million views, and fans started talking about it. Brown took matters into his own hands and shared a heartfelt message to Gio and commented on the video.

"It's ok lil bro ❤️ we will always be friends," he wrote.

And about eight weeks after the heartfelt exchange, both of them were recently reunited during Brown's farewell party .

However, now with the 76ers , Brown will join Philadelphia alongside LeBron James, Joel Embiid, and Tyrese Maxey. With the 2026-27 NBA regular season kicking off on October 20, they will face the defending champion New York Knicks in the season opener.

articles.title: El dardo de González Fuertes a los vídeos de RMTV: “No me parecen normales, pero nunca los vi"
articles.standfirst: El exárbitro aseguró en 'La Tribu' que nunca vio esas piezas durante su etapa en activo, pero dejó clara su postura: “¿Qué me aporta a mí eso?”
articles.summary: El exárbitro aseguró en 'La Tribu' que nunca vio esas piezas durante su etapa en activo, pero dejó clara su postura: “¿Qué me aporta a mí eso?”
articles.body: Pablo González Fuertes fue uno de los protagonistas de la mañana en La Tribu de Radio MARCA. El exárbitro, nueva incorporación de la casa para acercar el mundo arbitral a los oyentes, repasó su trayectoria, explicó cómo vive ahora el fútbol desde fuera del césped y dejó una reflexión clara sobre uno de los temas más sensibles de los últimos años: los vídeos de Real Madrid TV. Preguntado directamente por esos vídeos, González Fuertes fue tajante al reconocer que nunca llegó a verlos durante su etapa como árbitro. “Los vídeos nunca los vi. Nunca”, aseguró. Una respuesta que sorprendió por la contundencia y que el propio excolegiado explicó desde su manera de protegerse del ruido exterior. González Fuertes admitió que no puede valorar el contenido concreto de los vídeos porque decidió no consumirlos: “No sé si están bien hechos o mal hechos. No sé si me gustan o no me gustan. No los vi”. Sin embargo, sí dejó clara su opinión sobre la existencia de ese tipo de piezas alrededor de los árbitros: “No me parecen normales, obviamente no me parecen normales”. El exárbitro justificó esa distancia con una pregunta directa: “¿Qué me aporta a mí eso?”. Durante la conversación, explicó que uno de los mecanismos habituales de los árbitros en la élite es aislarse del entorno para poder competir con normalidad. “Por muy fuerte que seas mentalmente, hay veces que la vorágine mediática es muy fuerte. ¿Cómo te aíslas? Pues no viéndolo”, señaló. Esa misma idea la trasladó al recuerdo de la final de Copa junto a Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea, una previa marcada por el enorme ruido mediático. González Fuertes aseguró que no vivió aquel contexto “de una forma muy dramática” porque estaba centrado en preparar el partido y alejado de todo lo que se decía alrededor. En su nueva etapa como comentarista de Radio MARCA, González Fuertes reconoció que la parte más complicada será hablar de compañeros que, en muchos casos, siguen siendo amigos. Aun así, defendió que se puede analizar una decisión arbitral con naturalidad siempre que se haga desde el respeto. “Pablo dice lo que piensa y habla con la mano en el corazón”, explicó sobre cómo cree que le ven sus compañeros. Para el asturiano, el error forma parte del arbitraje y debe normalizarse: “El error hay que normalizarlo. Otra cosa es que ese error conlleve faltas de respeto”. El excolegiado insistió en que el fútbol se vive desde la pasión, pero pidió abrir el foco para juzgar al árbitro como profesional. “Tú puedes decir que, bajo tu punto de vista, es una cosa diferente a la que acaba de hacer el compañero o el amigo”, apuntó. González Fuertes también se pronunció sobre el caso Negreira, al que calificó como “el mayor escándalo de la historia del arbitraje”. El exárbitro recordó que él llegó al fútbol profesional cuando Negreira era vicepresidente del CTA y le describió como “un tío muy peculiar”. Sobre cómo debe cerrarse el caso, fue claro: “Si existe alguna persona que se haya vestido de árbitro que haya tenido algún tipo de relación, por pequeña que fuese, con este personaje de Negreira, que saliese a la luz”. Para recuperar la credibilidad del colectivo, González Fuertes pidió rebajar el clima de sospecha permanente. “Tenemos que empezar a desdramatizar esa vorágine que tenemos a nuestro alrededor”, defendió. Y cerró con una reflexión personal sobre lo que significa llegar a Primera: “En qué cabeza cabe que yo voy a dejar de vivir mi sueño por beneficiar a uno u otro”.

articles.title: England vs Pakistan second Test: Three talking points from cricket series
articles.summary: Pakistan’s batting collapses, concerns over the Lord’s pitch and Ollie Robinson’s rampant form highlight the series.
articles.body:
England clinched a Test cricket series victory over Pakistan with a thumping 194-run win in the second match of the tour at Lord’s Cricket Ground in London.

Pakistan, set an improbable victory target of 389, were dismissed for 194 on the fourth day to give England an unbeatable 2-0 lead in a three-match series on Sunday.

Ollie Robinson did the damage again with 4-24 to follow his sensational 4-11 in 13 overs during Pakistan’s woeful 110 all out in the first innings. Saud Shakeel restored some self-respect for Pakistan with 97 before he holed out to fast bowler Josh Tongue, who saw off the tail.

Victory saw England, who hammered Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley last week, complete their first multi-match Test series win since a 2-1 triumph in New Zealand more than a year ago.

Here are three talking points that emerged as England completed their first multi-match Test series win in more than a year.

Pakistan have yet to make 200 in this series, with the tourists dismissed for 171 and 135 during an innings and 103-run defeat in the first Test at Headingley before managing 110 and 194 at Lord’s.

But that Pakistan, already bottom of the World Test Championship table before this latest thumping loss, at least got close to a benchmark total on Sunday was largely down to Saud Shakeel’s enterprising 97.

Coming in with Pakistan in dire straits at 14-3, he initially scored briskly without taking undue risks before a flurry of thrilling boundaries, including two superb hooked sixes off fast bowler Josh Tongue, took him to within sight of 100.

Shakeel fell just short of what would have been his fifth century in 25 Tests when he holed out off Tongue, the left-hander failing to join Abbas on the Lord’s honours boards following the veteran seamer’s five-wicket haul earlier on Sunday.

“In the batting, we weren’t up to the mark [in the first innings],” said Babar Azam, the Pakistan captain. “Saud Shakeel showed his class and dedication in the second innings.”

The present England management have sometimes given the impression the only thing that matters in a pace attack is sheer speed, but Ollie Robinson has demonstrated the importance of accuracy and movement as well.

Robinson lacks the express pace and physical threat of Sussex and England teammate Jofra Archer. But the seamer’s range of skills was on display at Lord’s where, albeit helped by a green-tinged pitch, Robinson was named player-of-the-match for a haul of 8-35 that included a remarkable 4-11 in 13 overs during Pakistan’s first innings.

While concerns over his fitness and questions regarding some social media posts have threatened to derail his England career, there have rarely been any doubts over the 32-year-old Robinson’s talent.

In his three Tests this season he has taken 23 wickets at a stunningly low average of 8.34, with England skipper Joe Root saying on Sunday Robinson was “horrendous [to face] in these conditions.”

The way England opener Emilio Gay fell lbw for 31 to a ‘pea-shooter’ delivery from Pakistan paceman Mohammad Abbas was the kind of dismissal that really should not happen on the third day of a Test and certainly not at a ground that styles itself as the Home of Cricket.

For Gay, struggling to cement his place in the England side, it was a particularly cruel exit as what should be a game of skill was turned into a lottery by uneven bounce.

It was also a worrying sign for Marylebone Cricket Club, the owners of Lord’s.

The pitch for the previous Test at Lord’s, against New Zealand, was rated as “unsatisfactory” by the International Cricket Council, with next year’s World Test Championship final relocated across London to the Oval partly as a consequence.

And while previous surfaces at Lord’s, renowned for its steep slope across the ground, faced criticism for being bland and too much in favour of the batsmen, clearly there are limits.

MCC recognised they had an issue after the New Zealand match, announcing the creation of “an agronomy advisory group” and a “phased pitch-relaying programme”, although any benefits may not be seen for several years and are unlikely to be of much consolation to Gay.

articles.title: Venus Williams bows out of US Open with straight-sets defeat to Sofia Kenin
articles.summary: The 46-year-old US veteran loses to wildcard compatriot but will play in women’s doubles with sister Serena Williams.
articles.body:
American wildcard Sofia Kenin beat 46-year-old compatriot Venus Williams 6-2, 7-6(6) in a ⁠⁠US Open first-round match ⁠⁠that began past midnight in New York, the latest start in women’s tournament history.

The match at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday got under way after Novak Djokovic’s loss to Mariano Navone in five sets , with a sizable contingent of fans staying on well past midnight for one more look at Williams, who was playing as a wildcard in her 96th career Grand ⁠⁠Slam main draw appearance.

“It was extremely late,” Williams told reporters. “I’ve never played a match that late before, and I was happy to see that so many people stuck around for that. It was a real honour to play in front of them.”

Kenin broke serve in the opening game and never trailed ‌‌in the first set, racing to a 3-0 lead as both players struggled to find their rhythm, combining for nine double faults.

Williams, cheered on by chants of “Let’s go Venus”, broke back to love to trim the deficit to 3-1 but dropped serve again as Kenin pulled away to close out the set.

Kenin reeled off three straight games to lead 3-1 in the second set, and while Williams showed flashes of the form that earned her seven ⁠⁠Grand Slam titles, she struggled to string points together, with her second ⁠⁠serve proving especially costly.

Kenin saved four break points to level at 5-5, leaving Williams screaming in frustration at handing her opponent another game with unforced errors. However, Williams still found a way to hold for 6-5 before Kenin forced ⁠⁠a tiebreak.

Williams appeared to have the upper hand in the tiebreak but could not convert any of her seven set points, as Kenin dug ⁠⁠in to close out the win.

“It’s not ideal,” Williams said. “I ⁠⁠would have preferred something else, definitely. It wasn’t great for either of us, so I think we both tried our best.

“I just don’t know any other sport where you have to start that late. I definitely think there’s room for improvement there.

“It’s ‌‌not easy to do in the first round. It’s not easy to do it at 1 or 2 in the morning to try to find your rhythm and play your best, ‌‌but ‌‌I tried my best.”

Kenin, the 2020 Australian Open champion, will next face top-ranked American Jessica Pegula.

Meanwhile, former champion Daniil Medvedev and Pegula ⁠⁠advanced with little fuss earlier in the day, as players began their campaigns to grab a slice of the record prize purse of $108m up for grabs.

Russian Medvedev had crashed out in a chaotic first-round defeat a year ago but was all business on Sunday at Arthur Ashe Stadium, downing French qualifier Hugo Gaston 6-4, 6-2, 6-4 to quieten doubts after a frustrating run-up to the tournament.

“The last couple of weeks were not easy,” said Medvedev, who exited the Cincinnati and Montreal tournaments early. “I’m happy that today ⁠⁠I managed to produce high-level tennis.”

Dozens of ticketholders were lined up long before the action kicked off, and the home crowd was rewarded as world number three Pegula beat Romania’s Elena-Gabriela Ruse 6-3, 6-2 in the first match ⁠⁠at the showpiece stadium.

Twice Grand Slam champion Barbora Krejcikova earlier became the first seeded player to exit the tournament, saving six match points before succumbing to Kamilla Rakhimova 7-6(4), 6-2 on the outer courts.

Italian Jasmine Paolini survived a scare to beat Slovenia’s Veronika ‌‌Erjavec 6-3, 3-6, 6-4 in the opener at Louis Armstrong Stadium to set up a meeting with compatriot Lucrezia Stefanini.

Czech Jiri Lehecka kicked off the action on the Grandstand with a 6-1, 7-6(5), 4-6, 6-2 win over Spain’s Pablo Carreno Busta before Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk swatted aside Australian Storm Hunter 6-4, ‌‌6-1 ‌‌at the same stadium.

Kostyuk was joined in the next round by compatriot Elina Svitolina, who eased past Solana Sierra 6-1, 6-2.

Former champion Marin Cilic and 2022 runner-up Casper Ruud pulled out due to injuries shortly after the tournament got under way.

articles.title: Manchester United supporters left baffled as Old Trafford roof STILL leaks despite whopping $200M+ summer spending
articles.summary: International Sports News: Manchester United fans have been left frustrated after the leaky roof at Old Trafford caused problems again during the 5-2 Premier League win over Ips.
articles.body: Manchester United fans have been left frustrated after the leaky roof at Old Trafford caused problems again during the 5-2 Premier League win over Ipswich Town. Heavy rain led to water pouring through the stadium roof, with a waterfall-like flow visible around the Stretford End.The issue has raised fresh questions about the condition of the 116-year-old stadium. United have spent more than £150million ($203m) on new players this summer, while also investing in other stadium upgrades. However, the roof continues to leak during heavy storms, leaving supporters wondering why the long-standing problem has not yet been fixed.Old Trafford roof leak causes fresh concern for Manchester UnitedThe heavy downpour during Manchester United’s game against Ipswich Town once again exposed the problems with the Old Trafford roof.Water could be seen rushing from the roof at the Stretford End. It fell towards the ground below and created the appearance of a waterfall inside the stadium.Videos shared on social media also showed water leaking from other parts of the ground. Some footage appeared to show water dripping into areas close to the seating.The latest incident has surprised many United supporters. The club had the summer break to carry out major work on the stadium. Yet the roof problems remain.One fan posted, “Old Trafford’s roof is still leaking in 2026. New managers. New signings. Same waterfall.” While another wrote, “Man United just spent £150m this summer but the Old Trafford roof is still leaking.”A third commented, “Old Trafford waterfall sighting.” A fourth wrote, “It is 2026 and Old Trafford continues to leak when it rains.” Another fan added, “Well, that is why we want to build another stadium.”The complaints come at a time when United have spent heavily on their playing squad.The club have reportedly paid £70m ($95m) for Carlos Baleba, £50m ($67m) for Andrey Santos and £35m ($47m) for Youri Tielemans. Their total summer spending could also rise above £200m ($270m) if they complete another signing before the transfer deadline.Despite the major investment in the squad, the condition of Old Trafford remains a major talking point.The stadium has suffered from infrastructure problems for years. Heavy rain has previously caused water to enter different parts of the ground. Areas around the Stretford End and away dressing rooms have also been affected by leaks.United have considered work on sections of the roof in the past. Plans have included replacing parts covering the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand.However, a major decision over the stadium’s future could influence how much money is spent on the existing roof.The club are considering whether to carry out a major redevelopment of Old Trafford or build a completely new stadium. This has made extensive repairs to the current roof more complicated.United have still invested in other improvements this summer. The hospitality section has been extended. The pitch has also been replaced for the first time in 14 years.But the latest leak has reminded fans that major structural issues remain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Trey McKinney becomes youngest Bassmaster Angler of the Year at 21, breaking Kevin VanDam's record
articles.summary: Evan Kung won the St. Lawrence River tournament, but Trey McKinney stole the show as the youngest Angler of the Year in Bassmaster history at 21.
articles.body: CLAYTON, NEW YORK — Evan Kung's name is on the tournament trophy from the St. Lawrence River. But the biggest story out of Clayton this week might actually be the young guns. The Bassmaster Elite at St. Lawrence River closed out the 2026 Elite Series regular season, and with it came the season-long Angler of the Year and Rookie of the Year titles. These are awards decided by cumulative points across all nine regular-season events — not by who wins this one tournament. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Still, a lot was riding on how this Championship Sunday shook out. McKinney finally slays the dragon Trey McKinney came into the season finale having watched Chris Johnston walk away with the Angler of the Year title for two straight years — runner-up finishes that, as the emcee pointed out, meant McKinney had "never been out of the top two" in the AOY race in his young career. This time, the roles reversed: Johnston himself handed McKinney the trophy. A passing of the torch, you could call it. At 21, McKinney is now the youngest Progressive Bassmaster Angler of the Year in history — breaking a record held by Kevin VanDam since 1992. It's a fitting cap to a week where McKinney also boated the heaviest five-fish smallmouth limit ever weighed in Bassmaster history (30 pounds, 11 ounces, back on Day 2) and picked up his own Century Belt for good measure. None of it came easily. McKinney finished the tournament in second place, 2 pounds behind Kung. But by his own account, that was never really what he came to Clayton for. "Yes, I didn't win the tournament, but I wasn't even thinking about that," McKinney said. "Angler of the Year is the only thing I was thinking about all week. I was doing well in the tournament, but that title is what was on my mind." EVAN KUNG WINS BASSMASTER ELITE AT ST. LAWRENCE RIVER IN A TOURNAMENT FOR THE RECORD BOOKS The final push very nearly didn't happen. McKinney described his last hours on the water as the most nervous he's ever been fishing. "I was more nervous today than I've ever been in my whole life," he said. "I couldn't even think straight. My fish were short-striking, not committing, and I thought there was no way I was about to hand this away. We kept running around, and thank goodness, right at the end we caught a 6-pounder to seal it. "I was about ready to leave when something told me to keep going a little longer. There was one rock. I gave it a shot, and it was a 6-pounder. If I hadn't caught that fish, I don't think I would have gotten it." McKinney credited three years of hard work finally paying off. His mom took the mic on stage afterward to share in the moment, crediting faith and the support of everyone who'd backed him through the chase. Rookie of the Year was decided from the shore While McKinney was closing out his tournament, a tight Rookie of the Year race was being decided, too. And it included a man who wasn't fishing at all. Caleb Hudson led the rookie points race most of the season but didn't make the cut for Championship Sunday at St. Lawrence. This left him to watch from land as Fisher Anaya — the only other rookie still in contention — fished for the title. Anaya needed a top-six finish on the final day to overtake Hudson. He came in ninth, at 100 pounds, 5 ounces (a Century Belt, but not enough to flip the race), which meant Hudson held on to win Rookie of the Year without ever making a cast that day. "It was the most nerve-wracking day I've ever had to go through," Hudson said before the final leaderboard was announced. "I think today has felt like at least 30 hours long since I got up this morning. I'm ready for this to be over. I hate this feeling. Either way, I'm going to be happy. I've had an amazing season, and Fisher's a great angler. I'd have no problem losing to him. He's phenomenal." When it was official, Hudson — who picked up a $10,000 bonus check from Pro Guide Batteries along with the title — noted the timing: "Today's my mom's birthday, so I did it for her. Best birthday present — saves me some money on a gift." JACK STORY SKIPPED HIS HIGH SCHOOL GRADUATION TO GO BASS FISHING AND WALKED AWAY WITH $100K Anaya, for his part, lost the title in dramatic fashion — losing what he described as one of the biggest smallmouth of his life on his first two casts of the day. "What a battle, what a season," Anaya said. "The last two days have been rough. I've lost more than I've caught. I knew heading out this morning it just didn't feel right. Congrats to Caleb. It was his time to win, and he had a heck of a season. I'm not mad about losing to him. If it was going to be someone, he's the guy to lose to." Maybe we’re seeing a changing of the guard. articles.title: Cardona Reveals Gruesome Injury Details, WWE Rumors on Cathy Kelley's Future, Latest on Piper Niven
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

Matt Cardona's WWE comeback was halted by a devastating triceps injury, and the 41-year-old opened up about how things played out.

Cardona posted an Instagram video explaining the gruesome details of his injury, which first arose during his match against Gunther on the Aug. 14 episode of Friday Night SmackDown earlier this month.

"I got powerbombed on the announce table, got powerbombed on the apron twice and in the ring. My elbow was bothering me, but I didn't really think anything of it," Cardona said (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News).

However, further damage was done when Cardona tried to fight through the pain during a match against Kit Wilson at the Aug. 21 WWE Main Event taping.

"I felt a pop, and I thought, 'There's no way I hurt my elbow on a dropkick, right?'" he said. "I had no strength in my right arm. I said, 'Okay, this triceps is torn.' I could just tell."

Cardona underwent an MRI the following day that confirmed his triceps was completely torn off the bone. He had surgery on Aug. 25, and he rued the timing of his injury.

"Sure enough, yes—torn right off the bone, right off the elbow," he said. "It just sucks getting hurt now when I'm still figuring out who Matt Cardona is in WWE."

Cardona added that he's still motivated to make his WWE comeback memorable, and he won't let his injury deter him from his ultimate goals.

"Five months, six months, three months off at this point in my career—that's a long f--king time. I don't want to sit home. I don't want to sit and collect a check. I don't want to have a vacation. I want to be in the ring," he said. "I came back to win the WWE Championship. I might sound crazy to you, maybe I'm delusional, but that's just how I'm wired. I will not die. I am a cockroach—whatever you want to say. I love this stuff too damn much to let this injury stop me. I'll be back faster than the surgeon said and coming back to be the WWE Champion—or I'm going to die trying."

WWE Reportedly Considering Expanding Cathy Kelley's Role

Cathy Kelley has long been WWE's go-to backstage correspondent, but it sounds like she could be taking on more responsibilities soon.

According to a recent report from WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select, WWE is looking at other ways to use Kelley after being impressed with her work over the last few months.

"It has been relayed to us that WWE has been impressed as of late with the work of Cathy Kelley and that the company would like to find additional roles for her outside of her current backstage correspondent position on television," the report stated (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News). "Kelley, who by all accounts is well-liked and extremely engaging, has stood out over the course of the last few months."

Kelley worked for WWE from 2016 to 2020 before returning to the company in 2022. The company is reportedly considering including her in its digital promotions.

"We're told WWE has considered making her a focal point of upcoming social media campaigns while also having her take on a significant role within the social aspects of Club WWE," the report stated. "The feeling within is that WWE sees an opportunity to utilize Kelley's strengths beyond her current television role and continue expanding her presence across the company's digital platforms."

Kelley previously told Chris Van Vliet in an interview that she isn't particularly interested in testing her skills in the wrestling ring, but she would be open to a manager role at some point in her career.

For now, it appears that Kelley will continue to be featured as one of WWE's lead personalities on the broadcast side.

Piper Niven has been absent from WWE for over a year after suffering a serious neck injury, but she provided a positive update on her progress.

Niven shared on Instagram that she's 12 weeks removed from neck surgery, and her scans showed that she's healing properly.

"Got my 12 week scans and everything is 'healing beautifully,'" Niven wrote in her caption (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News).

Niven last wrestled in August 2025. In June, she confirmed that her surgery recovery has an indefinite timeline, and there's a chance she may not be able to wrestle again.

Still, Niven decided to keep things optimistic as she thanked fans for checking on her. She also warned that she won't be back on social media frequently, as she's content with focusing on her recovery.

"I logged into a tonne of messages of love and concern and I wanted to say thank you so much," she wrote. "I am probably not gonna get back to anyone before I Irish goodbye back out of social media, please don't hate me. But thank you all for giving a hoot. Imma go back to living my geriatric Florida bam life."

Fans will certainly continue to hold out hope that Niven can make a full recovery, and it sounds like she's already on the right track.

articles.title: AEW All In vs. WWE WrestleMania, Which Show Was Best Spectacle of the Year?
articles.summary: In the midst of what has been a banner year for All Elite Wrestling, the pressure was on for All In 2026 to deliver and it ultimately did not disappoint.
articles.body:
In the midst of what has been a banner year for All Elite Wrestling, the pressure was on for All In 2026 to deliver and it ultimately did not disappoint.

Although the attendance at Wembley Stadium in London was considerably lower than what the inaugural installment did in 2023, the show still boasted nearly 50,000 fans and featured an incredible card from top to bottom.

AEW's creative direction largely being consistent throughout the year has had a positive impact on attendance at various events, viewership and general buzz surrounding the product.

It's especially interesting to compare the company's growth this year to what WWE has been doing, specifically with the mixed feelings fans have had toward the product despite the big business they continue to do.

WrestleMania 42 in particular was a significant talking point in the wrestling world back in April for a variety of reasons, and with WrestleMania and All In being the biggest events of the year for WWE and AEW respectively, it's expected for them to be compared to each other.

Criteria to determine which show was the best spectacle of 2026 so far will include the layout, pacing, atmosphere, in-ring action and memorable moments from each event.

WrestleMania expanding from one to two nights starting in 2020 was among the smartest moves WWE has ever made with The Show of Shows. The cards were simply becoming too bloated and tedious to justify keeping them at only one night.

It allows WWE to add more matches to 'Mania without tiring out the live crowd. All In has always been a one-night event, but All In 2026 was surprisingly shorter than the average AEW pay-per-view (not counting the two-hour pre-show) due to the curfew that London has in place and the show needing to end before a certain time.

There were certainly points during All In where the Wembley Stadium crowd was exhausted from all of the wrestling, but they came alive when it mattered most, including down the stretch for the top two main events.

It started hot with The New Level debuting and progressed nicely from there, culminating with the best bout of the night in Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay. The layout was terrific with everything being positioned right where it should have been.

Meanwhile, Night 2 of WrestleMania 42 was noticeably stronger than Night 1, at least in terms of how it was executed. The two-night formula still works for WrestleMania, but there needs to be a better balance in the amount of attractions allocated to each night so one doesn't overshadow the other.

The pacing of AEW's pay-per-views is normally the biggest knock against them from fans. The wrestling never fails to deliver, but the vast amount of matches combined with the excessive length of each one almost always results in marathon shows.

All In was oddly an exception to that, and not only because of the earlier start time. Other than the Trios title fiasco overstaying its welcome, every match lasted about as long as it needed to, right down to the AEW Women's World Championship and AEW World Championship main events being able to breathe without being dragged out or rushed.

Unfortunately, WWE's new premium live event model with minutes of commercials airing in between each other simply isn't sustainable. It drastically hinders the flow of the show and forces many matches to get cut for time, even at WrestleMania.

That was especially an issue on Night 1, but WWE did improve upon that with Night 2. Most of the undercard received a decent amount of time and the 30-minute-plus instant classic for the World Heavyweight Championship closed out the weekend on a high note.

A happy medium between the two pacing styles would be ideal, but between these two specific shows, All In had more of a seamless stride.

There will eventually come a point where AEW won't be able to run All In at Wembley Stadium annually anymore. It may be years down the road, but All In being held in the same stadium year after year is bound to lose its luster and that will affect attendance.

Until then, though, it will remain an epic atmosphere, which in turn gives every match on the show a big fight feel. As previously noted, the crowd won't be white-hot for every single thing that happens, but if the pacing is consistent throughout, it will blow almost every other event AEW does during the year out of the water.

Of course, that's been the case with WrestleMania since its inception, and regardless of whether it's critically acclaimed or poorly received by fans, it has always felt larger than life. Even when certain matches have under-delivered, the stage and setup alone make the show special.

All In 2026 and WrestleMania 42 were essentially the same in that regard. All In featured a ton of unique entrances from Kenny Omega, Will Ospreay, Willow Nightingale, Kevin Knight and others. The walkouts at WrestleMania for CM Punk, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes and Liv Morgan were all pretty breathtaking as well.

All In being back at Wembley for the first time in two years was fun, but Las Vegas just didn't need WrestleMania two years in a row and that was yet another factor in the fan fatigue toward the event.

It is possible for there to be too much of a good thing and wrestling pay-per-views aren't immune to that. More often than not, AEW pay-per-view cards have way too much wrestling and it causes certain matches to get lost in the shuffle.

Again, though, All In seemed to take the "less is more" approach (at least with the main card) and it worked out wonderfully. There were nine matches in the four-plus hours and virtually everything (with the possible exception of Jon Moxley vs. Nigel McGuinness) felt like it was worthy of AEW's grandest stage.

The undercard had several standout matches and the top two main events will be included in the conversation for the very best of AEW in 2026.

The in-ring action at WrestleMania 42 was enjoyable on the whole, but many matches were shorter than they should have been and therefore didn't get a chance to be more than what they were. Gunther vs. Seth Rollins and Rhea Ripley vs. Jade Cargill were above average and CM Punk vs. Roman Reigns was an absolute gem, but the rest of the card on the two nights left a lot to be desired.

The wrestling at All In was far superior to what WrestleMania delivered in April.

WWE prides itself on giving fans a surplus of "WrestleMania moments" every year. Although the latest installment was by no means perfect, there was no shortage of special moments between the two nights.

In fact, the moments may have eclipsed the matches at 'Mania by a wide margin this year with Paige returning to the ring, Bianca Belair announcing her pregnancy, Oba Femi essentially squashing Brock Lesnar, IShowSpeed going viral, Danhausen sharing the screen with John Cena, multiple championships changing hands and much more.

AEW has officially embraced All In being its premier pay-per-view and it's treated it as such in recent years. At the 2026 event alone, Will Ospreay and The Brawling Birds captured gold in their home country, The New Level debuted, Sting returned, and Mercedes Moné clinched the AEW Women's World Championship.

This is another category that All In and WrestleMania are virtually even in. The overall feedback to All In was significantly more positive online, but WrestleMania 42 was a definite improvement over the mixed bag that was WrestleMania 41 and it still offered enough satisfaction for fans.

The moments will be remembered just as much as the matches will be, maybe more so, and both events had a historical impact in their own way.

WrestleMania 42 wasn't the weakest WrestleMania WWE has produced in the last decade, but it also paled in comparison to the 'Mania events in 2023 and 2024 when the company was creatively firing on all cylinders.

If anything, the event served as an additional reminder of how corporate and commercialized the product has become as well as what can be fixed and avoided for future installments. It was one of WWE's better premium live events of 2026, yet it wasn't the complete package that All In was.

Every installment of All In that AEW has done to date has ranged from fun to fantastic, but All In 2026 was practically a perfect pay-per-view with a wide variety of styles, stories and surprises. Not every booking decision was the right one, but there was very little for fans to complain about once it was over.

Fans who enjoyed WrestleMania over All In are well within their rights to do so, and there will always be those who will prefer the pacing and structure of the shows that WWE puts out over AEW's. However, All In provided the better bang for the viewer's buck and a more exciting experience for the audience in attendance.

AEW once again outdid itself with another exceptional All In, but that isn't to say WrestleMania can't bounce back with a stronger show next year if it learns from this year's mistakes and puts together the thrilling card fans know it's capable of.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: NHL Power Rankings for Every Team Heading Into September 2026
articles.summary: It's official: NHL hockey starts next month.
articles.body:
It's official: NHL hockey starts next month.

The league's 2026-27 season begins with multiple games on Sept. 29 and the 32 teams will run an 84-game gauntlet for the first time since 1993-94.

The Carolina Hurricanes bear the enviable burden of arriving as reigning Stanley Cup champions, having defeated the Vegas Golden Knights in six games in June.

The B/R hockey staff has greeted the news with another set of Power Rankings to put some order to the league as it reaches its get-started month.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

It's all about the R word in Vancouver this season.

Though the haul the team got for Quinn Hughes was impressive, it likely won't amount to much more than a blip on the standings radar.

The Flames may be, just may be, on the far side of the process.

They've dumped a number of high-end veterans since their last playoff appearance in 2022 and have reaped the benefits of having a young goalie in Dustin Wolf, who's amassed 52 wins across the last two seasons.

A bevy of premium draft picks could continue to bolster the pipeline or perhaps entice a willing partner into a trade for a bigger name player.

GM Kyle Davidson is doing some good things in his own version of a franchise rebuild, but it doesn't help that the centerpiece of that process, Connor Bedard, won't be available for the season's first month.

Bedard had surgery on his left shoulder after an injury sustained during summertime work in Vancouver in early July.

Not only did Davidson get Bedard locked down for the long term with a five-year, $75 million contract, but he also returned prodigal son Patrick Kane to Chicago and acquired defenseman Bo Byram in a trade with Buffalo.

Will all that yield a first Cup parade since 2015? It's doubtful, but it should make the stretch from September to April a little more interesting.

Cheat Sheet to Every NFL Team's Backup QBs

Breaking down winners and losers from NFL cut day

It's never a good look when a player aiming for a big contract turns down a bag full of cash from your franchise.

But that's the treatment the Kraken got earlier this summer when Jason Robertson rejected a trade that would have sent him to Seattle with an eight-year deal worth about $15 million annually.

Instead, Robertson, a restricted free agent, stayed in Dallas on a one-year pact worth $12 million.

Three straight years of NHL irrelevance doesn't help a team attract players.

The press release officially hit the fan when longtime goalie Connor Hellebuyck went public with what had been a private trade request.

Assuming the 33-year-old doesn't change his mind before shuffling off to Buffalo or New Jersey or parts unknown, his exit leaves the goaltending chores in the hands of ex-Oiler Stuart Skinner, who had a 2.99 goals-against average and an .885 save percentage in 27 starts with Pittsburgh after a December trade.

Hellebuyck, in what figures to be his final season in Winnipeg, won 23 games alongside a 2.86 GAA and an .895 save percentage in 57 starts.

His three Vezina trophies, though they've yielded zero appearances in the Stanley Cup Final, are tops in the league among active goalies.

An era ended when the Rangers sent Artemi Panarin to Los Angeles.

But perhaps the second act began when the New York brass acquired Pavel Dorofeyev from Vegas for three draft picks in June.

For those unaware, the 25-year-old Russian winger is coming off consecutive 30-plus-goal seasons with the Golden Knights in which he actually totaled 72.

Add in a top-flight goalie in Igor Shesterkin and the ingredients for a relevant winter are there.

Steve Yzerman's gone as GM, but Dylan Larkin is still a Red Wing.

The latter probably isn't a great sign for the locker room this fall considering Larkin, as the team's captain, went public with a trade demand.

But while unloading the final five years of an $8.7 million annual contract might be good for the front office and dispatching the bad mojo might help team morale, Larkin is still a No. 1 center and they don't grow on trees.

He's exceeded 30 goals for five straight seasons and netted a career-best 34 in 2025-26.

What that's meant recently is three playoff misses in the last four seasons and precisely one series win, in 2022, since they hoisted the Cup in 2019.

A 37-33-12 record was only good for fifth in the Central and 22nd overall last season, and the summertime acquisitions of Mason McTavish and Connor McMichael don't figure to change that reality by much.

Center Robert Thomas remains in the fold after a point-per-game effort, 64 points in 64 games, in 2025-26.

If you're looking for a team that's hit on a recent No. 1 overall pick, look no further than the Islanders.

Matthew Schaefer was snatched with the first choice in the 2025 draft and rewarded the confidence with a Calder Trophy season in which he not only charmed the fan base but put up 23 goals and 36 assists on the ice.

Problem is, while Schaefer is still a teenager, more than half of the 14 forwards on the New York roster are beyond 30 and the team's leading scorer last season, Mat Barzal (72 points), was 46th in the league.

Even one of the league's elite goalies in Ilya Sorokin doesn't make up for that.

The regime has changed, but we're still waiting on the Predators.

The free-agent frenzy that brought Steven Stamkos, among others, a few years back still hasn't yielded a playoff series win, instead generating two straight playoff misses.

Nashville was above .500 at 38-34-10 last season but was only good enough for sixth in a loaded Central Division and hasn't won a playoff round since 2018.

Newcomers this year include Jack Drury, Ross Colton and Mavrik Bourque but Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly and Roman Josi aren't getting any younger.

There's plenty to like in Columbus. The Blue Jackets are talented up and down the roster and a compelling watch on the ice.

Like Detroit, though, it doesn't help when the best player, in this case Norris Trophy-winning defenseman Zach Werenski, seems he'd rather be elsewhere.

Reports early in the summer suggested Werenski blocked a trade to Dallas and that he'd told the Columbus brass he'd not sign a long-term deal with the team, but recent weeks have included a public makeup. We'll see.

Like the Blues a few places earlier, here are the Kings.

A sound team. A competent team. A team that's been good enough to reach the playoffs after each of the last five seasons.

But they lost in the first round all five times, four in a row to Edmonton from 2022 to 2025, and then in a sweep by Colorado last spring.

Will a full season of Panarin along with new coach Peter Laviolette and some other tinkering change all that? Perhaps. But given the opposition elsewhere in the Pacific Division and the West as a whole, it's unlikely to be by much.

The Devils pulled the plug on the Jacob Markstrom goaltending experiment after just two seasons, sending the $6 million (annually) man to Florida for Evan Rodrigues, Jesper Boqvist and Ben Steeves in late June.

Markstrom was 23-19-1 with a 3.07 goals-against average and an .883 save percentage in 44 games last season, and his exit means Jake Allen, 36, is the No. 1 man after going 17-17-2 in 37 games alongside Markstrom.

Outside the goal crease, defenseman Simon Nemec and forward Maxim Tsyplakov are gone to Calgary in a deal that landed three picks and defenseman Etienne Moran.

But let's face it, the Devils will live and die on the health of forward Jack Hughes, who's not played more than 62 games in a season since 2022-23 but has been a point-per-game producer for five seasons in a row.

Will the real Pittsburgh Penguins please stand up.

The aging Penguins had missed the playoffs for three straight seasons before a 2025-26 resurgence in which they amassed 98 points, finished second to Carolina in the Metropolitan Division, and reached the postseason only to be bounced by cross-state rival Philadelphia.

It's been relatively quiet on the Steel City front all summer though they did bring in Andrei Kuzmenko as a free agent and Nick Robertson from Toronto in a trade that cost a fourth-round draft pick.

Stuart Skinner signed with Winnipeg and left the goal crease to the largely unproven pair of Sergei Murashov (22 years old) and Arturs Silovs (25 years old). Are they enough to keep Sidney Crosby relevant as a 39-year-old? Stay tuned.

One summer they let Mitch Marner walk out the door.

The next, they take a three-year, $21 million flyer on a 37-year-old goalie coming off the worst statistical season in a career that reaches back to 2010-11.

Yep, it's another chapter in Toronto Maple Leafs history.

Still, dismiss the Leafs as a worthy commodity at your own risk. They've still got talent up front and if "Bob" is anything like what he was during Florida's two Cup-winning seasons, particularly in the playoffs, it'll be a relevant season in Ontario.

The Sharks haven't made the playoffs since 2019 and missed out on a Western Conference spot last spring by just four points.

But GM Mike Grier has been busily trying to address things. He's already got the league's burgeoning superstar in Macklin Celebrini up front, but the player-turned-executive has worked on the blue line all summer.

Darnell Nurse arrived from Edmonton with an annual $9.25 million cap hit that runs to 2030. Free agent Jacob Trouba signed a four-year, $33 million deal. And Michael Kesselring is in town from Buffalo after Grier got him for three years and $13.5 million.

Is a gigantic, pricey defense the key to getting Celebrini to play deep into the springtime? We'll have to wait and see.

If you're looking for a young team poised to make a competitive step out West, look no further than the Anaheim Ducks.

The Ducks squeaked into the playoffs and did damage upon arrival, eliminating the two-time defending conference champion Oilers in the first round before being squashed by Vegas in Round 2.

Their salary structure was thrown out of whack by an offer sheet that'll keep Leo Carlsson in town for five more years at $18 million apiece, but having a defenseman like Jackson LaCombe under wraps through 2034 doesn't hurt.

Make no mistake, the Flyers are a sound team that does a lot of things well.

They were ninth in the league in goals-against average last season, allowed the fourth fewest shots per game, and won a playoff series for the first time since 2020.

But their leading scorer, Travis Konecny, was tied for 55th in the league, which seems to indicate the need for a game-changing top-end player in the forward group.

They tried to get one with the aforementioned offer sheet to Anaheim's Leo Carlsson, but once the Ducks matched it left GM Daniel Briere to consider other options.

The Senators were already on the list of young NHL teams on the rise, and they should remain so even after the summertime departure of Brady Tkachuk to Florida that yielded four draft picks in return.

Ottawa was fifth in the Atlantic Division and snatched a playoff berth last spring before finding themselves on the wrong end of a sweep by the eventual champion Hurricanes.

Tkachuk took his 37 goals and 71 points with him to South Beach, but the Senators still boast the likes of Tim Stutzle (24 years old), Shane Pinto (25), Dylan Cozens (25) and William Eklund (23) up front, and each is signed through at least the end of the 2028-29 season.

Will it be enough to get past the equally upwardly mobile likes of Buffalo and Montreal? Perhaps not. But Canada's capital should be a hockey relevant city all season.

Like Pittsburgh in the Metropolitan Division, Boston was the surprise team in the group last season, amassing 100 points after missing the playoffs a season before.

It didn't yield anything more than a first-round exit against Buffalo, but it did indicate buy-in to the system implemented by first-year coach Marco Sturm.

Winger JJ Peterka is new to the group after a draft-day trade from Utah, which cost Boston a pair of draft picks. Peterka has scored 20-plus goals in three straight seasons and has rung up 35 power-play points during that stretch.

It's been a long time since Phoenix, eh?

The franchise formerly known as the Coyotes reached the postseason in its second season in Utah—its first playoff berth since 2020—and enters 2026-27 boasting one of the league's deepest cores of young talent.

The Mammoth tied for third in the Pacific last season and were just three points off the pace of division-leading Vegas, finishing in the top half of the league in scoring average, goals-against average, and wins.

Arriving this season are Vincent Trocheck (trade from the Rangers) and Anders Lee (free agent from the Islanders), and also back is leading scorer and point-per-game man Clayton Keller, who had 26 goals and 62 assists in 82 games.

The puff of smoke above Capital One Arena means only one thing.

Alex Ovechkin will return for a 22nd season of NHL hockey.

The 41-year-old Russian, who now doubles as the league's all-time goal-scoring leader, is apparently invigorated enough by the franchise's offseason maneuvering to give it another go in a career that stretches back to 2005.

Adding guys like Boone Jenner, Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou to a forward group will do that for a guy.

"Look at our roster," Ovechkin said . "We have a Stanley Cup contender. I know I can still play. I know I still can bring energy to the locker room and energy on the ice."

So, you thought the Oilers were desperate to win a Cup before?

Welcome to the Mike Babcock Experience, Circa 2026.

Edmonton's brass insists the team's leadership—read: Nos. 29 and 97—signed off on the hire and wants to be coached hard. But we'll see how that holds up when they lose three straight in late November.

The Sabres went from a decade-plus of darkness to Atlantic Division champions last year, but were still unable to deliver the city its first top-tier championship.

Instead, though Buffalo toppled rival Boston in the first round it was beaten, on home ice in Game 7, by Montreal in the second and ended a 50-win, 109-point season with a sour taste.

A young and presumably still hungry group returns for 2026-27, though Alex Tuch took the money and ran to Washington, Bo Byram was dispatched to Chicago and Devon Levi is part of a three-goalie blueprint in Edmonton.

All five of Buffalo's top forwards are in their 20s and signed through at least 2028-29, not to mention D-men Rasmus Dahlin (26) and Owen Power (23), who'll be in Western New York for the long term as well.

Minnesota finished seventh overall in the NHL with 104 points but was just third in a loaded Central Division behind Colorado and Dallas.

The team ended a 10-season run of either first-round exits or playoff misses last spring, defeating the Stars in six games in the first game before a five-game exit at the hands of the Avalanche in Round 2.

Minnesota has not gone beyond the second round since a run to the Western final in 2003 yielded a loss to eventual Cup-runner-up Anaheim.

Now, the focus is on defenseman Quinn Hughes, whom Minnesota acquired from Vancouver in December and who is set to become a free agent after this season.

There's good news and bad news in Dallas.

The good news is that the Stars were not eliminated in the Western Conference Final for a fourth consecutive season.

The bad news is that their season ended much sooner in 2025-26, with a six-game first-round loss to the Minnesota Wild.

The team remains loaded, but it'll be consistently interesting to see how it handles the return of Jason Robertson, who was inked to a one-year deal after turning thumbs-down on a would-be trade to Seattle.

Robertson's return could remain a distraction.

They're not the team that went to three straight Cup Finals from 2020-2022, right?

But they're also not a team destined to lose in the postseason's first round, as they've done for four straight seasons since Colorado claimed the Cup in 2022.

So, will the real Tampa Bay Lightning reveal themselves?

There's enough of the old Cup-winning guard around to advance to April on muscle memory alone, and newer arrivals like Jake Guentzel, a Cup winner in Pittsburgh, can more than pull their weight when it comes to winning postseason hockey. So, pencil the Lightning in for the tournament and stand back.

The Western Conference boasts a handful of young teams that are clearly on the rise and it's not as if the East's cupboard is bare when it comes to that description.

But none are more qualified to lead the charge than Montreal.

The Canadiens ended a three-year playoff drought in 2025 and made their presence felt this past spring, eliminating division mates Tampa Bay and Buffalo in seven games apiece before running into the eventual champs from Carolina.

If they don't win it all at least once in the next five years, fold the franchise.

They've not been around long, but the Vegas Golden Knights have nevertheless established that the one guarantee about the franchise is that nothing is guaranteed.

They fired coach Bruce Cassidy with eight games remaining in a Pacific Division-winning season, then rode interim coach John Tortorella to the Stanley Cup Final before showing the 68-year-old the door in favor of Ryan Craig.

Craig, 44, has never been a head coach above the AHL level, but he's well aware of the standard set by his predecessors.

"As for expectations, we're going to go about our business day in and day out with the goal in mind to continue to build, stack and get better each and every day," he said , "so that we have an opportunity, when the calendar flips in mid-April, to compete for the trophy."

But it's not so bad to be the recently deposed two-time champs, either.

Florida's quest to become the first team to win three straight Cups since the Islanders of the 1980s fell short thanks to myriad injuries and other factors, but it's hard to suggest the Panthers aren't reloaded for another title chase in 2026-27.

They replaced Sergei Bobrovsky with the younger, less expensive Jacob Markstrom, will return Aleksander Barkov after a year on the shelf, and acquired all-world agitator Brady Tkachuk to come in and play with his equally irritating brother, Matthew.

Hockey people already knew Cale Makar is the real deal.

But the defenseman proved it to the bean counters, too, with an eight-year, $163.2 million contract that makes him the league's first $20 million (annual) man.

He's only been an NHL'er for seven seasons but Makar has already copped a Stanley Cup and a Conn Smythe Trophy, not to mention a Calder and two Norrises.

Sure, the Avs are down to less than a million in cap space, but having the likes of Makar, Nathan MacKinnon and Martin Necas locked up for several years still seems to guarantee long-term relevance in the Rockies.

Nothing better than entering September as the defending champs, right?

The Hurricanes didn't make any earth-shattering acquisitions over the summer and nor did they lose any vital pieces, perhaps outside of veteran goalie Freddie Andersen, who's gone to Edmonton.

It's not titillating, but what it mostly means is that the group that rolled through the playoffs on a 16-3 tear after winning its division by a wide margin returns nearly intact.

Good news for Raleigh, but bad news for everyone else.

articles.title: Inside how Los Angeles Lakers billionaire icon Magic Johnson’s Starbucks gamble changed his life, paving the way for a $200 million LA Dodgers fortune
articles.summary: International Sports News: Magic Johnson has built a huge business empire since retiring from the NBA. The basketball legend made some of his biggest gains through smart investm.
articles.body: Magic Johnson has built a huge business empire since retiring from the NBA. The basketball legend made some of his biggest gains through smart investments. One of his most successful ventures was his partnership with Starbucks, which eventually helped him invest in the Los Angeles Dodgers.Johnson used money from the Starbucks deal to become part of the Dodgers ownership group in 2012. He invested $50 million of his own money in the baseball franchise. The Dodgers are now valued at around $8 billion, making his sports investment worth far more than it was when he bought in.How Starbucks helped Magic Johnson build his enormous sports empireMagic Johnson’s journey into business began long before his Los Angeles Dodgers investment.While he was still associated with the NBA, he started building businesses through Magic Johnson Enterprises. His goal was to invest in companies that served communities that were often overlooked by major brands.One of his biggest moves came through Urban Coffee Opportunities, his partnership with Starbucks.Johnson built Starbucks stores in urban neighbourhoods. Instead of taking profits from each store, he reinvested the money to expand the business.“So, what I did with Starbucks, I let the first one build the second one,” he said per The Sun.Johnson eventually sold his 50 percent interest in Urban Coffee Opportunities in 2010. The deal reportedly earned him between $75 million and $100 million.That money later helped him enter professional sports ownership.“I sold Starbucks, and who would have ever thought that the Dodgers would be for sale? So I used the money that came back to me from the Starbucks sale, and put it into the Dodger deal”, he added.Johnson joined Guggenheim Baseball Management in the $2.15 billion purchase of the Dodgers in 2012. He reportedly invested $50 million personally.The investment has become extremely valuable. The Dodgers are now estimated to be worth around $8 billion. Based on Sportico’s valuation, Johnson’s stake is worth about $200 million.The Dodgers are only one part of Johnson’s sports portfolio.He also has ownership interests in the Los Angeles Sparks of the WNBA, Los Angeles FC of MLS, the Washington Commanders of the NFL, the Washington Spirit of the NWSL and esports organisation Team Liquid.His investment success extends beyond sports. Johnson has also been involved in movie theatres, fitness centres, real estate, energy and finance. articles.title: 4 WWE Storylines We'd Build for the Rest of 2026
articles.summary: Only four months remain in 2026, but there's plenty of potential for storylines to impact WWE positively and set it up for a big 2027.
articles.body:
Only four months remain in 2026, but there's plenty of potential for storylines to impact WWE positively and set it up for a big 2027.

From substantial character changes to the unleashing of a werewolf, they are stories that can propel the company forward at a time of year in which the WWE product typically becomes somewhat stagnant and prepare it for the all-important road to WrestleMania.

What are those stories? Let's take a look.

It has become clear that The Vision is firmly a midcard act. No longer the show-dominating faction it once was, it's time for Bron Breakker to free himself from the group and embark on a singles run toward the main event scene.

After wrapping up his battles with Oba Femi over who the true future of WWE is, he can realize that he is better than his current situation and break free from The Vision, embarking on a babyface run that sees him tear through Austin Theory and engage the returning Bronson Reed in a short program.

By the time December rolls around, he should be clear from the group and preparing for a sizeable push toward bigger and better things, with the WWE Universe ready to shower The Badass with cheers and dog barks.

We have already seen Jacob Fatu's willingness to stand on his own and disobey The Bloodline when he sees fit. We watched it happen when Roman Reigns condescended to him, leading to The Samoan Werewolf standing back and watching LA Knight and Solo Sikoa get the better of his family.

Already a fan-favorite for the intensity he brings to his performance and the ass-kicking nature of his character, it will not be difficult to get Fatu back over as a main event-level babyface.

The build should continue through the end of the year, with Reigns disrespecting Fatu and treating him as a foot soldier rather than a member of the family. Fatu could even endure a beatdown at the hands of The Bloodline for his transgressions.

Let the fans build a little sympathy for Fatu so that when it is time for him to defy Reigns and unleash hell, they are ready to see The Samoan Werewolf tear stuff up.

It would put him on course to be free of the group and set up a rematch with Reigns in which he is the indisputable hero and ready to fight against the oppressive world heavyweight champion, with a chance to take the gold.

This one may be more fantasy booking than a real possibility, but it is time to pull the trigger on a Cody Rhodes heel turn.

We had our first taste of Rhodes fatigue earlier this year, when the boos started to outweigh the cheers on the road to WrestleMania 42, and the result was one of the most polarizing main events in the history of The Showcase of the Immortals.

Rhodes has worked too hard to become the face of the company to suffer the fate of the latest top babyface rejected by a bored or disinterested audience.

The seeds have already been planted, too. We have witnessed the frustration mounting as Rhodes is separated from the Undisputed WWE Championship. He has become edgier, even ruthless at times, and is hell-bent on regaining the prize, which leaves no doubt that he is QB1.

He has resisted calls for a heel turn in the past as the top babyface and hero to millions, but the last thing anyone wants to see is Rhodes become a caricature of the hero; a guy booed in favor of others because the fans are tired of seeing him shake hands and kiss babies.

Using the current rivalry with Orton, and growing tension between him and Punk as the catalyst, a Rhodes heel turn at an event such as Survivor Series: WarGames in Houston would not only freshen him up, but also give fans something to buzz about at a time of year that is usually not particularly hot for the company.

A bitter Rhodes who lets out all of his frustration on the audience, after years spent being the hero it deserves, is a character fans could easily be excited about and WWE could build on.

Damian Priest Betrays R-Truth, Re-Enters Title Picture

This past Friday night on SmackDown, WWE Creative laid the groundwork for a Damian Priest heel turn when he expressed a desire to split from R-Truth and embark on a singles run back to the top of the company.

While he gave in to his tag team partner and agreed to one more match as partners, The Archer of Infamy has the chance to make a definitive statement.

Imagine a scenario where, frustrated over another loss, Priest snaps and brutalizes Truth. The good thing about having someone so beloved by the fans is that he is an effective tool when it comes to getting someone over as a villain.

From there, Priest can go on a tear that rejuvenates him.

A Superstar with great presence but fell into a bit of a rut over the last year, he could be heated right back up and inserted into a packed WWE title picture, ready to reestablish himself as a main event presence.

articles.title: El Valencia empieza a dar miedo
articles.standfirst: Codere ya lo sitúa como uno de los tantos candidatos al descenso
articles.summary: Codere ya lo sitúa como uno de los tantos candidatos al descenso
articles.body: Apenas tres jornadas han bastado para que las casas de apuestas empiecen a mover con fuerza el mercado de descensos en LaLiga, y el nombre que más está llamando la atención es el del Valencia. El conjunto de Mestalla suma un solo punto de nueve posibles y arrastra una imagen cada vez más preocupante, con dos derrotas y un empate que dejan a los ches instalados en la zona baja de la clasificación. El calendario no ha ayudado, pero tampoco las sensaciones. El Valencia empezó empatando 0-0 ante el Celta en Mestalla, un resultado discreto pero no alarmante. Sin embargo, todo se torció después. En el partido aplazado de la primera jornada cayó 0-1 ante el Betis, también como local, con un gol de Pablo García a ocho minutos del final. Y el pasado domingo llegó el golpe más duro, una derrota por 3-1 en Riazor ante un recién ascendido Deportivo que fue muy superior. Los goles de Aubameyang, sumados a dos autogoles de César Tárrega y Mouctar Diakhaby, retrataron a un equipo desordenado atrás y con serias dudas defensivas, pese al recorte de Sadiq. Esa imagen, más que el resultado en sí, es la que ha disparado las alarmas. Codere ha reaccionado bajando la cuota del descenso del Valencia hasta 7, una cifra que lo sitúa ya al mismo nivel que Getafe y Celta. Lo más preocupante para el Valencia es que ahora tiene dos partidos muy complicados, lo que le hará más difícil salir de la parte de abajo. Este fin de semana recibe al Barcelona y la próxima jornada viaja hasta el Pizjuán para medirse al Sevilla. Pese al mal inicio valencianista, Codere mantiene su tridente de favoritos para perder la categoría. En primer lugar aparece el Málaga, a cuota 2.05, tras encajar un severo 4-0 ante el Real Madrid en el Bernabéu en la última jornada, que se suma a las dificultades ya mostradas en su regreso a Primera. Le sigue el Racing de Santander, a 2.65, pese a haber logrado su primera victoria de la temporada por 3-2 ante el Elche gracias al triplete de Zabiri; un triunfo que, de momento, no ha bastado para que Codere modifique en exceso su percepción sobre el recién ascendido. Cierra el podio el propio Elche, a cuota 2.75, después de esa derrota en El Sardinero que certifica el irregular comienzo de los franjiverdes, que hasta ahora solo habían sumado puntos ante Deportivo y Barcelona. Lo llamativo del movimiento de Codere no es tanto que el Valencia aparezca en la porra del descenso, sino la velocidad con la que ha bajado su cuota. Pasar a compartir cifra con Getafe y Celta, refleja que el mercado empieza a leer el mal inicio valenciano como algo más que un simple bache.

articles.title: Predicting the Chicago Bears' 2026 practice squad
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears will soon begin assembling their practice squad. Here are our predictions for who will make the cut.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have formed their initial 53-man roster , cutting a number of players in the process . Unfortunately, that meant a lot of good players were released.

General manager Ryan Poles will soon start assembling his 16-player practice squad, which can include up to six players with more than two accrued seasons, beginning Monday after the waiver process has concluded. The practice squad serves as an extension of the active roster, which will provide depth at certain positions.

There are a number of players that Chicago waived or released during roster cuts who are expected back on the practice squad, and they could also turn to other players who cleared waivers or were released across the league.

Before the Bears start building their practice squad, here are my early predictions:

When can the Bears start forming their practice squad?

The Bears can start forming their practice squad starting at 11 a.m. CT on Monday, Aug. 31.

How many players are on the practice squad?

In previous seasons, teams were allowed to carry 10 players. That number was going to expand to 12 for the 2020 season and then expand to 14 in 2022. That changed with COVID-19, where the league increased practice squads to 16 players, which will once again be the limit in 2026. Teams can have a 17th practice squad member as part of the International Pathway Program (IPP). Of those potential 17 practice squad members, 10 must have two or fewer accrued seasons. The other six do not have any limitations and are classified as "veterans."

Any player can sign with a team's practice squad, but there are limitations in place. Here are the different categories for practice squad players, according to Sporting News .

Rookies, or players who have not accrued one season of NFL experience

Any player who was not active for more nine regular-season games or more during their accrued seasons

A maximum of four players who earned no more than two accrued NFL seasons

Six players who have accrued more than two NFL seasons.

At least one player who is a member of the NFL's International Pathway Program (IPP)

How much do practice squad players make?

There are two different salary scales for practice squad players depending on a player's experience. There's one for players with two or fewer accrued seasons (which are most practice squad players) and one for everyone with three or more, according to Sporting News .

The first group, which includes rookies and players who have played no more than two accrued seasons, receive a fixed weekly salary of $13,750. The second group, which consists of players who have played three or more accrued seasons, do not have a fixed salary. The minimum weekly salary for a veteran on the practice squad is $18,350, while the maximum is $22,850.

How can a practice squad player be signed away?

Players on a team's practice squad are free to sign with another team at any point. Although, a team that signs a player from a practice squad must add the player to its 53-man roster. That means no switching practice squads across the league.

How can teams utilize practice squad players each week?

Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players on game day, per Sporting News , expanding their roster to 55 players. Seven players will be designated as inactive. Following the game, players who were elevated to the game day roster revert back to the practice squad. Practice squad players can only be elevated two times per season. If a team wants to play them more, they must sign them to the active roster.
