articles.title: ‘Social media player’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer brutally tears into Babar Azam after Lord’s horror show
articles.summary: Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali strongly criticized captain Babar Azam following another batting failure. Azam's recent Test performances and lack of centur...
articles.body:
Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali has launched a strong criticism of Babar Azam after the Pakistan captain endured another disappointing outing in the second Test against England at Lord's. Pakistan suffered a 194-run defeat on Sunday to concede the three-match series 2-0, with their batting once again failing to withstand pressure. Chasing 389 in the fourth innings, Pakistan were bowled out for 194, while Babar managed only six after scoring eight in the first innings. For Basit, Babar's latest failure raised a much bigger question about his contribution when Pakistan need him most. Speaking on The Game Plan show, Basit compared Babar with several legendary Pakistan batters, arguing that the country's greatest players established their reputations by delivering in difficult situations. "They didn't become great players just like that. I'm not even talking about Sachin Tendulkar. I'm talking about my own countrymen". Basit then questioned whether Babar has done enough when Pakistan have been under pressure. "When you don't do anything in difficult times, what's the point? You're a great player in your fan following. You're a great player in front of social media."

The former batter then directly turned his attention to Babar and highlighted his long wait for a Test century. Babar's last Test hundred came in December 2022, when he scored 161 against New Zealand in Karachi. Since then, he has been unable to reach three figures in the format. "When will you do it? I'm talking about Babar [Azam]. I'll take his name. He hasn't scored a [Test] hundred in four years. When will you do it?" Basit said. He also expressed his frustration at Babar's dismissal at Lord's, particularly because Pakistan's batting heavily relied on their captain to provide a substantial contribution. "It's a matter of pain. When the entire country's batting depends on you. At least don't get out by hitting such a shot," Basit lamented. Babar's dismissal came early in the chase when he got into trouble against Jofra Archer. The Pakistan captain attempted to leave a short delivery but ended up offering a simple catch to Jordan Cox in the slip cordon.

Basit did not spare the other Pakistan batters either. Saud Shakeel provided the strongest resistance during the chase, scoring 97 off 132 balls and helping Pakistan recover after they slipped to 14/3. However, his attempt to accelerate towards a century ultimately cost him his wicket. After smashing two sixes in an over from Josh Tongue, Shakeel fell three runs short of his hundred while attempting another aggressive shot. "I'm not even satisfied with Saud [Shakeel]'s shot. You've taken on five fielders and you're hitting such a shot," Basit complained. Mohammad Rizwan was another target of Basit's criticism after the wicketkeeper-batter scored only one before being dismissed lbw by Ollie Robinson. "What shot did [Mohammad] Rizwan hit? Doesn't he have any sense? Is he playing a Test match or street cricket?" Basit said.

Pakistan's problems with the bat were evident almost immediately in their chase. Robinson dismissed Azan Awais lbw before producing a delivery that breached Abdullah Shafique's defence and hit the off stump, leaving Pakistan in serious trouble. Archer then removed Babar, and Pakistan went into lunch with Saud Shakeel and Shan Masood attempting to rebuild. Shakeel eventually reached his fifty from 54 balls and formed a useful partnership with Masood. But Robinson returned after the rain interruption to dismiss Masood, before removing Rizwan soon afterwards. With Imam-ul-Haq unavailable to bat because of his calf injury, Pakistan's hopes were effectively over. Shakeel continued fighting but fell on 97, with Tongue then wrapping up the tail. England's bowlers dominated the final innings, with Robinson finishing with eight wickets in the match, as Pakistan were dismissed for 194. The defeat leaves Pakistan 2-0 down in the series, with the third and final Test to be played at Edgbaston in Birmingham from September 9.

articles.title: Breaking down the 2026 Penn State football team position-by-position
articles.summary: Matt Campbell grew up in northeastern Ohio, played for the legendary Larry Kehres at Mount Union and learned from such coaches as Jim Tressel. So it’s no sur...
articles.body:
Matt Campbell grew up in northeastern Ohio, played for the legendary Larry Kehres at Mount Union and learned from such coaches as Jim Tressel.

So it's no surprise what Campbell wants from the Penn State offense in his first season as head coach.

"We want to be physical," said offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser, who has worked for Campbell since 2015 at Toledo and then Iowa State. "We want to win the line of scrimmage. Be nasty. Be violent. That has to be the mentality here."

Mouser, though, has had a knack for making unexpected calls since he became a coordinator in 2024. He's been described as fearless and aggressive.

"We want to be different," he said. "We want to be able to do things that no one expects us to do and throw tendencies off. Everyone thinks second and short is a shot downfield. We want to run it on second and short. We'll take a shot on second and long."

The Nittany Lions offense will have an Iowa State flavor. Mouser, quarterbacks coach Jake Waters and offensive line coach Ryan Clanton came from the Cyclones, along with six expected starters, most notably quarterback Rocco Becht.

Here's a position-by-position breakdown of the offense going into Campbell's first season at Penn State:

Becht was the most important transfer that Campbell landed after his hiring, not only because they're familiar with one another but because Becht has so much experience.

Going into this season, he leads all Football Bowl Subdivision quarterbacks in games played (42), starts (39) and career snaps (2,509). He also has passed for 9,274 yards, second among all active FBS quarterbacks, and 64 touchdowns, which is tied for third. He's a dynamic leader with a magnetic personality.

It's imperative that Becht stay healthy, though. Highly regarded redshirt freshman Alex Manske also transferred from Iowa State, but he missed spring practice after undergoing open-heart surgery. He's been medically cleared, but he doesn't have much experience.

Connor Barry, a transfer from Division III Christopher Newport, took most of the practice snaps in the spring because Becht was limited while recovering from offseason surgery and Manske was out.

Bottom line: Becht is a perfect fit for Mouser's offense and a clutch player.

Kaytron Allen and Nick Singleton finished their careers as the No. 1 and No. 4 leading rushers in school history, combining for more than 7,600 rushing yards. Following them will be difficult.

Carson Hansen, another transfer from Iowa State, has the most experience. He led the Cyclones in rushing the last two seasons, running for 1,771 yards, 19 TDs and a 4.9 per-carry average in his career.

He'll be joined by James Peoples, a former four-star prospect who rushed for 541 yards in two seasons at Ohio State, and Quinton Martin Jr., also a one-time four-star prospect who rushed for 103 yards in Penn State's Pinstripe Bowl win over Clemson.

Bottom line: All three might share the load because Campbell wants to be a power team.

The position mostly has been deficient for the Lions since Jahan Dotson's spectacular college career ended in 2021.

Former Penn State coach James Franklin tried in vain to improve the wide receivers through recruiting, the transfer portal and often changing position coaches.

Campbell brought Brett Eskildsen and Chase Sowell with him from Iowa State after they combined for 62 receptions, 1,026 yards and seven touchdowns last season.

Eskildsen, one of the fastest players on the team, averaged a team-high 17.5 yards per catch; Sowell was named the Big 12 Offensive Newcomer of the Year after he transferred from East Carolina.

Speedy sophomore Koby Howard, who had a strong second half last season for the Lions, will be the third wide receiver. Don't discount young receivers like Zay Robinson, Karon Brookins and Amarion Jackson or Grambling transfer Keith Jones Jr.

Bottom line: This might finally be the year that Penn State receivers can create separation.

This might be the deepest position on the roster with Ben Brahmer, Andrew Rappleyea and Gabe Burkle leading the way.

All three are adept at blocking and receiving. They combined for 83 catches for 928 yards and 10 touchdowns last season.

At Iowa State, Brahmer caught a team-high 37 passes for 446 yards last season and Burkle had 26 catches for 302 yards and one TD. Rappleyea made 20 receptions for 180 yards for Penn State and had a TD catch in each of the last three games.

Bottom line: Expect the Lions to use formations with two, three and even four tight ends.

Brock Riker appears to have won the job to succeed Nick Dawkins, the starter the last two seasons.

Riker was a Freshman All-America second-team pick who started 12 games last season at Texas State and allowed no sacks.

Dominic Rulli, a former Penn State walk-on, played mostly on special teams until he started against Clemson in the Pinstripe Bowl. He's expected to be the backup.

Bottom line: Riker was among Campbell's first targets in the portal.

Replacing first-round draft pick Vega Ioane will not be easy, but Cooper Cousins and Trevor Buhr give Penn State two solid blockers.

Cousins was a highly rated prospect coming out of high school who played in every game as a freshman in 2024. But he was slowed by injuries early last season before he made two starts.

Buhr made 12 starts the last two seasons without allowing a sack. He received All-Big 12 honorable mention last year.

Will Tompkins and Vaea Ikakoula, a pair of freshmen, are expected to be the primary backups.

Bottom line: Cousins and Buhr have big shoes to fill, but seem up to the task.

Anthony Donkoh will return to right tackle, his more natural position, after starting at guard last season. Donkoh had injuries each of the last two seasons and missed spring practice this year.

If he can stay healthy, he could be one of the better offensive linemen in the Big Ten.

Malachi Goodman, a four-star recruit in 2025 who did not play last season, has impressed Campbell and Clanton since their arrival and is the top candidate to start at left tackle. Garrett Sexton, Owen Aliciene and Kuol Kuol will be in the mix.

Bottom line: Expect Donkoh to have a better season and Goodman to make an impact.

Campbell and defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn sought to make the front four bigger in order to stop the run and succeeded.

The top four tackles – Siale Taupaki, Keanu Williams, Dallas Vakalahi and Armstrong Nnodim – all weigh at least 310 pounds and are all transfers. Taupaki and Williams are the likely starters.

Penn State has some talented and promising ends, including returners Max Granville and Yvan Kemajou and transfers Ike Ezeogu and Alexander McPherson.

Campbell moved linebacker Caleb Bacon to end in order to bolster the pass rush because he's the only lineman who had more than two sacks last season.

Bottom line: Finding a consistent pass rush from guys up front will be paramount.

This position is much deeper than it was at Penn State last season with as many as five guys capable of significant playing time.

Kooper Ebel, Tony Rojas and Cael Brezina will be the starters when the Lions are in a 4-3 alignment. Ebel tied for the Iowa State lead in tackles last season and is a two-year starter. Rojas suffered a knee injury in practice after four games last season and has surprised his coaches with his quick recovery.

Alex Tatsch and Cam Smith also have impressed coaches.

Bottom line: Ebel and Rojas are versatile players who could line up anywhere.

Penn State returns Audavion Collins, Zion Tracy and Daryus Dixson at cornerback, at least on paper. They could line up at any of five positions in the secondary. Collins enjoyed a terrific fall camp.

Keep an eye on freshmen Jahmir Joseph and Josiah Zayas.

At safety, Iowa State transfers Marcus Neal Jr., Jeremiah Cooper and Jamison Patton, along with Vaboue Toure give the Lions plenty of depth. Neal and Cooper, who's coming back from a knee injury last September, are projected to be future NFL players.

Bottom line: They're not getting much preseason love, but the D-backs could be very good.

The importance of Ryan Barker's decision to return to Penn State has been overlooked by some.

Barker tied for the national lead in field goal percentage last season, making 18-of-19 kicks for a .947 percentage. He's the most accurate field goal kicker in school history.

The Lions will have a new punter, Mississippi State transfer Nathan Tiyce or freshman Lucas Tenbrock, and a new long snapper, Blaise Sokach-Minnick.

Peoples, Martin and Howard are the top candidates to return kickoffs; Howard, Tracy and Robinson are competing to be the punt returner.

Penn State also blocked five kicks last year under coordinator Justin Lustig, who has stayed with the Lions.

Bottom line: Penn State hopes the punters and the returners are as dependable as Barker.

articles.title: Rocky Colavito remembered as a baseball star and a dad
articles.summary: To Steve Colavito and his older brother and sister, their father, Rocco D. “Rocky” Colavito, never seemed like a celebrity. The late major league baseball pl...
articles.body:
To Steve Colavito and his older brother and sister, their father, Rocco D. "Rocky" Colavito, never seemed like a celebrity.

The late major league baseball player and coach was just their dad.

"Everybody knew him as a baseball player, but my dad, to me, was just the best dad there was," Colavito said in a recent interview. "He always made time for me. Always. It was never too much for my dad."

His words echoed those of his sister, Marisa McGrath, during a tribute Aug. 11 at FirstEnergy Stadium, where the siblings and their mother, Carmen Colavito, gathered with family, friends and fans to celebrate the late ballplayer's career and life.

As a girl, McGrath said, she did not understand all the fuss made over her father by the teachers when he brought her and her older brother, Rocky Jr., lunch at school or the hospital staff when she cut her foot and needed stitches.

"I just knew my dad was there," she said.

The tribute took place before the Reading Fightin Phils faced the visiting Chesapeake Baysox on the diamond at 1950 Centre Ave.

The evening's first 2,500 ticket holders received a limited edition Rocky Colavito bobblehead created for the occasion.

Matt Hoffmaster, assistant manager of the Fightin Phils, said the idea grew from a relationship that developed between the organization and the family after Colavito's death in December 2024 at age 91.

Colavito's celebration of life was held at the stadium's Redner's Event Center, Hoffmaster explained, and members of the Fightin Phils management kept in touch with the family, eventually planning the tribute.

For many, Hoffmaster said, the setting carried special meaning.

In 1953, before becoming one of Major League Baseball's power hitters, Colavito played in the then-2-year-old Reading Municipal Memorial Stadium — dedicated to military personnel killed in service — as a member of the Cleveland Indians organization, which brought a minor league affiliate to Reading a year earlier.

Although affiliations changed over the ensuing decades, the stadium endured, with the Philadelphia Phillies establishing a feeder team in Reading in 1967.

The venue recently underwent a $45 million upgrade and expansion as part a new deal between Major League Baseball and minor league teams like the Fightins.

Some of the fans who watched Colavito play in Reading were able to return to the same ballpark to honor him 73 years later, Hoffmaster said.

"You can't find many professional baseball stadiums where Rocky Colavito and teammates of his era played," he said.

Colavito, who was inducted into the Reading Baseballtown Hall of Fame in 1993, went on from Reading to become one of baseball's premier players of the late 1950s and 1960s, said Mark Sommer, a Buffalo-based journalist and author of the 2019 biography "Rocky Colavito: Cleveland's Iconic Slugger."

Sommer said Colavito combined power at the plate with an exceptional throwing arm in the outfield and an ability to connect with fans.

Between 1958 and 1962, Colavito hit more home runs than any other major leaguer, tying for the American League lead in home runs in 1959, Sommer said, and surpassing such legends as Willie Mays, Hank Aaron and Roger Maris during that span.

At the height of his popularity in Cleveland, however, Colavito was traded in 1960 to the Detroit Tigers for American League batting champion Harvey Kuenn. The deal stunned Cleveland fans and became one of baseball's most controversial trades, Sommer said.

By the time Colavito retired in 1968, he ranked 15th in career home runs in major league history, the author said.

"In the context of the times in which he played, in the era that he came out of, he was absolutely one of the best players in baseball," Sommer said.

But Colavito's appeal went beyond statistics.

He was known for staying after games to sign autographs until every waiting fan had one, Sommer said. The slugger remained just as approachable decades later.

At a 2021 ceremony in Cleveland unveiling a statue in his honor, Colavito, then 88, stayed outside in the August heat, signing autographs for about two hours rather than disappointing fans, Sommer recalled.

Colavito's connection to Berks County continued long after his playing days in Reading ended.

A Bronx native, the ballplayer met his future wife, Carmen Perrotti, while playing here. The two married in October 1954 and reared their family of three children, Rocky Jr., Marisa and Steve in Muhlenberg Township.

The couple later moved to Bern Township.

For Steve Colavito and his siblings, their father's devotion to family means more than the home runs, accolades and baseball lore.

Colavito of Maidencreek Township recalled spending summers with his father in Cleveland when the elder Colavito was coaching. Night games meant late dinners, but when he wanted to return to the ballpark early the next afternoon, Colavito said his father never complained.

"He was always willing," he said. "His family meant the world to him."

Baseball also became part of Steve Colavito's life. He was drafted by the Baltimore Orioles and later played in the Cleveland organization. Through the difficult stretches of his own professional career, he said, his father remained a constant source of support.

"Whenever my dad was there, I always felt like Superman," he said. "I didn't feel there was anything I couldn't do or accomplish when he was there."

That paternal support extended to all aspects of his life, Colavito said.

"It went beyond baseball," he said. "He was just always there for me."

articles.title: Should Red Sox Call Up Player Returned From Rule 5 Draft To Start In Place Of Sonny Gray On Tuesday?
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox currently don't have a starter scheduled for Tuesday
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox are skipping Sonny Gray's start on Tuesday and need to decide who will start in his place.

The Red Sox could have a bullpen day, but they are in the middle of a 13-game stretch, and taxing the bullpen on just day five seems less than ideal. The rosters are set to expand on Tuesday, and interim manager Chad Tracy has noted the team will work through how they want to structure the rotation.

"We're just talking through what we want to do," Tracy said, per The Boston Globe's Tim Healey. "It's September and we're talking through, what do we want to do and how do we want to structure this rotation? … We'll get more information as we go."

The Red Sox could look to call up Jedixson Paez. They lost Paez to the Chicago White Sox in the Rule 5 Draft, but he was designated for assignment in April and had to be offered back to the Red Sox for a $50,000 fee. Paez pitched in three games for the White Sox, posting an 18.00 ERA.

For the Red Sox, he had a 4.59 ERA in 17 games in Double-A, including seven starts. In Triple-A, he has made three starts to the tune of a 2.92 ERA. According to MassLive's Chris Cotillo, he was listed as the WooSox starter all week for Sunday's game, but did not pitch. He would make sense as a call-up for a spot start. In his last Triple-A game, he threw five innings, allowing one earned run on one hit and striking out eight.

Tracy noted that Gray feels fine physically, and Gray agreed. However, the Red Sox are thinking ahead and getting him some extra rest as they eye October. The Red Sox have not clinched a berth yet, but it's not too early to start thinking about the pitching plan for the postseason.

articles.title: Bradley Barcola to Keep PSG Shirt Number with Liverpool
articles.summary: Barcola will keep the 29 he wore at Paris Saint-Germain and first picked because of a video game.
articles.body:
Liverpool have made their big signing of the 2026 summer transfer window, bringing in 23-year-old French international left winger Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal that could be worth up to £125M including add-ons.

As with any big new signing, one of the first questions many will have is which shirt number will the player wear. And on that front, the answer is 29.

Barcola will continue to wear the 29 he used for much of his time at PSG, which he chose as a result of playing the FIFA (now EA FC) career mode known as "The Journey" that was first in the 2017 edition of the game, where you controlled a player named Alex Hunter who goes on to wear the number.

Barcola has previously said as a result he always imagined wearing that number if he made it at the highest levels—and so then picked it with PSG and will continue to wear it with the Reds.

For those looking to get their Barcola kit as quickly as possible, Liverpool's new left wing star will also continue to have "B. Barcola" on the back of it as he did at PSG.

articles.title: Gabe Ikard makes bold interception prediction for Courtland Guillory
articles.summary: Gabe Ikard boldly predicts Oklahoma safety Courtland Guillory will lead the SEC in interceptions in 2026.
articles.body:
The 2025 college football season introduced some new stars to the Oklahoma Sooners . One of those was freshman cornerback Courtland Guillory.

Guillory started from the opening game due to an injury to Eli Bowen. Then, when Bowen returned from his injury, Guillory proved he was too good to take off the field. He finished the year with 41 tackles, one tackle for loss and seven pass deflections. He and Bowen formed one of the best cornerback duos in the SEC last season.

Heading into this year, in his series of bold predictions, former Oklahoma All-American Gabe Ikard believes Guillory is in for a major season in the Crimson and Cream.

"My last prediction: I think you're going to like this one," Ikard said on 'The Oklahoma Breakdown with Ikard and Lehman.' "He didn't have an interception a season ago, but Courtland Guillory will lead the SEC in interceptions. May sound a little strange because he didn't have one last year. But I just feel like I have such high expectations for him this year. Also, he's going to be challenged."

It's a massive prediction for a player who didn't record a single interception last season. The leader in the SEC was at just four. But there is an important distinction: Ikard isn't predicting Guillory will suddenly become a completely different player. He's betting that the flashes he showed as a freshman will translate into more opportunities to make plays on the football.

That's where the "he's going to be challenged" part becomes important. If opposing quarterbacks are willing to test Guillory more often, he'll have more opportunities to turn pass breakups into interceptions.

The prediction is certainly bold, but Oklahoma may have the perfect environment for it. With Venables' defense returning plenty of talent, Guillory won't have to carry the secondary by himself. He just needs to turn his freshman flashes into game-changing plays.

And if he does, the zero in his interception column from 2025 could look very strange by the end of 2026.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic’s US Open defeat was tough to watch – the question he now faces is even harder
articles.summary: Djokovic appears set on finishing his career at the 2028 Olympics but he must decide whether he can stomach the painful scenes that accompanied his first-rou...
articles.body:
In the end, the end comes for everyone. And at the end, the end can be brutal; not a heroic rage against the passing of time and dying of the light, but in tears, doubling over with a cramp, and vomiting in the punishing New York humidity. Novak Djokovic was not just left facing the question of how long he has left to fight after his first-round exit from the US Open on Sunday night, but how many more times he could stomach the difficult scenes that accompanied his five-set defeat to Mariano Navone . "I pretty much despised every moment that I spent on the court," the 39-year-old said.

Djokovic has previously stated that he wants to keep playing until the LA Olympics in 2028, where he will compete under Serbia's flag for one last time. The dream of a record 25th grand slam title and the thrill of competition is what keeps his fight alive. It was only in January that Djokovic produced one of the greatest performances of his career in defeating Jannik Sinner in five sets in the semi-finals of the Australian Open, a night that vindicated his belief and continued pursuit. It is an achievement that looks all the more remarkable now after Djokovic admitted to an underlying health issue that is causing serious discomfort on the court. "Can the issue be fixed?" Djokovic said. "I don't know. I'm trying."

If it can't, and Djokovic's body continues to "collapse" in conditions such as a stifling late August night in New York, then the road to Los Angeles could become a long one. Though he continues to dedicate himself entirely to his physical conditioning, Djokovic is already essentially a part-time tennis player, concentrating solely on the grand slams and using the occasional tour event as a warm-up towards the biggest tournaments. He still reached all four grand slam finals in 2025 and was the third-best player in the world behind Carlos Alcaraz and Sinner, and then reached a grand slam final at the start of 2026. But the drop-off since Wimbledon – although he has only played two matches – has been alarming.

Djokovic's ranking will now fall outside of the world's top-10 for the first time since 2018, making his path in future grand slams even harder. So much had to fall his way already: managing his conditioning and staying injury-free, avoiding both Alcaraz and Sinner in the draw, and the odd stroke of luck such as Lorenzo Musetti's quarter-final retirement in Australia. At the US Open, with Sinner sidelined and Alcaraz only just returning from his wrist injury, Djokovic had what appeared on paper to be a golden opportunity , before the painful reality of attempting to become the oldest man to win a grand slam in history set in the final two sets of his defeat on Sunday night.

And yes, the words "painful reality" have been used to describe the challenges Djokovic encounters at grand slam many times since his last major title at the US Open in 2023. But there was pride and defiance on his way to successive semi-final defeats to Alcaraz and Sinner last season. Even at Wimbledon this year, his five-hour quarter-final victory over the third seed Felix Auger-Aliassime ranked as a vintage display . But the tears that welled up in Djokovic's eyes as the Arthur Ashe Stadium stood to cheer his solitary game in the fifth set against Navone, as he shuffled around the court and looked every bit his age? They were painful, and all too real.

Djokovic knew it, too. He is not the first and will not be the last great champion to face the reckoning that comes when their powers begin to wane, and their body refuses to answer. Djokovic "despised" it and likely gained nothing from it apart from perhaps a few more doubts to go along with the body-blow of how suddenly the end can appear. Ahead of 2027, the year where he turns 40, he could yet find comfort in reframing his expectations. But even doing that would be admitting to defeat. If Djokovic's physical issues are simply his age, it is a problem that has no remedy.

As tough as it was to watch Djokovic's defeat to Navone, there is every chance he returns in January at the Australian Open following several months of rest, recovery and preparation and once again proves everyone wrong by going deep into the tournament. But Djokovic's earliest grand slam exit since he was a teenager asks a question that will surely now follow him into the 23rd season of his career: how long he is prepared to accept being a diminished force, should he fall to another early defeat in Melbourne.

articles.title: Roma Increase the Level of Experience of Their Roster
articles.summary: Roma didn’t complete two deals they had set up last week, Jayden Oosterwolde and Morato, but they still got busy, signing Martin De Roon from Atalanta and Le...
articles.body:
Roma didn't complete two deals they had set up last week, Jayden Oosterwolde and Morato , but they still got busy, signing Martin De Roon from Atalanta and Leonardo Balerdi from Olympique Marseille.

The Giallorossi didn't finalize the deal with Fenerbahce because the fullbacks' injury was more severe than anticipated. They tried to change the terms, but in vain. They aren't tracking new options for now, as their youth product Emanuele Lulli has proven to be serviceable.

Roma didn't onboard Morato because Nottingham Forest insisted on an immediate permanent deal. Instead, the Ligue 1 side accepted a loan with a €15M conditional obligation to buy. He was no longer part of the plans after being a stalwart for 6 seasons and piling up 200 appearances.

The Giallorossi pounced on a similar situation with De Roon. Maurizio Sarri picked Gianluca Gaetano to anchor his new-look midfield. He asked out when his long-time gaffer came calling, and Atalanta didn't stand in his way. He'll replace Neil El Aynaoui, who's headed to RB Leipzig for a potential €29M package, Sky reports.

As for their frontline, they are working on Zenit's Luiz Henrique and Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling, Alfredo Pedullà reports. They could add a pair if Matias Soulé departs.

Our Take on Roma Signing De Roon and Balerdi

While El Aynaoui never quite fulfilled the potential he showed at Lens, it's manifest that they wanted to move on from every signing made by their previous director that wasn't signed off by Gian Piero Gasperini. Time will tell whether they'll regret some exits. In the meantime, they have played it safe with two known commodities who won't cause trouble and provide a solid contribution when called upon.

articles.summary: The latest updates in Italy confirm that Atalanta are closing in on an agreement to sign Jonathan Rowe from Bologna in a deal in the region of €40m on the pe...
articles.body:
The latest updates in Italy confirm that Atalanta are closing in on an agreement to sign Jonathan Rowe from Bologna in a deal in the region of €40m on the penultimate day of the summer transfer window.

Atalanta and Bologna on the verge of Rowe agreement

Atalanta have been targeting the signing of English winger Rowe for the final few weeks of the summer transfer window, and as a result of the recent speculation, the 23-year-old has been left out of the Bologna squad for their Serie A match on Monday, which just so happens to be away against Atalanta.

Domenico Tedesco confirmed on Sunday that Rowe was not in the best place to play on a mental level.

Now, according to reports from various outlets on Monday afternoon, Atalanta are closing in on a final agreement with Atalanta and are now discussing the final details of a deal.

La Dea look set to seal the deal at a guaranteed cost of €35m, plus €5m in bonuses and a 10% sell-on clause according to the latest updates from Gianluca Di Marzio .

Reports from Alfredo Pedullà suggest that Atalanta could send youngster Federico Cassa to Bologna as part of the transaction.

Liverpool are wrapping up significant transfer business before the deadline on Tuesday.

Bradley Barcola has put pen to paper on his Anfield contract following his £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain. And more wingers are likely to follow.

Deals are live for both Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh. Crystal Palace want £75m for 28-year-old Senegal winger Sarr while Minteh - currently injured - is valued slightly higher at £80m by his club Brighton.

In order to facilitate deals for Barcola and another winger outgoings are inevitable. Federico Chiesa may end up leaving for a club in Serie A while Harvey Elliott is wanted for a loan deal at Valencia.

And what about Cody Gakpo ? Reports emerged over the weekend that the 27-year-old forward wanted a move to Manchester City. Enzo Maresca's side have moved into lead to sign the Dutch international - who joined the Reds back in 2023 for around £37m.

He looks surplus to requirements now however with Barcola leading Andoni Iraola's attacking revolution.

Liverpool reject City's opening offer for Gakpo

An asking price of around £85m has been set for the versatile attacker - who is under contract until 2030 on wages of around £250k per week.

It's been claimed by a report in the Daily Mail that City have slid an opening offer across Richard Hughes' desk in a bid to land the former PSV captain.

Bayern Munich defender Hiroki Ito has been offered to Ajax by his management, according to Philipp Kessler .

The Japanese international is surplus to requirements on Vincent Kompany's side and could be in for a last-minute move to the Netherlands.

Ajax are considering a move for the central defender in order to strengthen their backline as they challenge for the Dutch title, which they haven't won since 2022.

Ito's current contract at Bayern runs until 2028, and it's unlikely that the 27-year-old will be offered a new contract. As per TransferMarkt , Ito's transfer value is around €18m.

articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA − Now that the Eagles have trimmed their roster from 90 players to the NFL mandated 53, the next step begins:

That is the forming of the practice squad. NFL teams are allowed 16 players on the squad, 17 if one is from the International Player Pathways program. The Eagles have that opportunity as both IPP alums Uar Bernard and Joshua Weru were waived on Aug. 30.

That process begins on Aug. 31 at 1 p.m. once waiver claims have cleared. If a player waived by one team is claimed by another, that player is on the 53-man roster of the claiming team. If a player is not claimed on waivers, then he is eligible to sign to any team's practice squad.

Keep in mind that more than 1,100 players were either waived or released on Aug. 30 as teams trimmed their rosters from 90 to 53.

A practice squad player is not allowed to play in games. That is, unless he is one of the two allowed game-day elevations. After the game, the player is returned to the practice squad. A player is allowed to be elevated three times during a season.

articles.title: The most frightening stat behind Aaron Donald’s return to the Rams
articles.summary: This Rams defensive stat became even scarier after Aaron Donald's return
articles.body:
Myles Garrett has a new running mate in Los Angeles. And another former Defensive Player of the Year at that.

Aaron Donald made it official on Sunday , ending weeks of speculation by announcing that he was indeed coming out of retirement to play for the Los Angeles Rams. Donald walked away from the game following the 2023 season despite continuing to play at a high level, as he recorded 8.5 sacks for the Rams during that final season.

With Garrett on the edge and Donald coming back along the defensive front, Los Angeles has a pair of standout pass rushers to put pressure on opposing quarterbacks.

But there is one stat, however, that should terrify the rest of the NFC.

This is a defense that was already rather good at getting pressure on opposing passers before Garrett arrived, and Donald returned.

As set forth in Aaron Schatz's FTN Football Almanac previewing the 2026 season, last year the Rams pressured opposing quarterbacks at a rate of 31% when sending the four standard pass rushers after the quarterback:

Jared Verse was part of that mix, yet he is now playing for the Cleveland Browns as part of the Garrett trade. Beyond Verse, however, the Rams called on players like Byron Young on the edge and Kobie Turner on the inside to help generate some of that pressure. Turner, for example, ranked fifth in ESPN's " Pass Rush Win Rate " statistic for defensive tackles.

Now Garrett and Donald are coming to help. Garrett ranked sixth in Pass Rush Win Rate among edge defenders a season ago, while Donald led all defensive tackles in that metric during the 2023 season , his last in the NFL.

The Rams have been our No. 1 team in the power rankings since the Garrett trade. LA is currently betting favorites to win the Super Bowl at +500 on FanDuel , while the next closest team, the Buffalo Bills, is +1000. Donald is 35 years old and hasn't played football in two years, which might lead you to lower your expectations for him. But he's also an all-time great who got to rest his body for two years before returning the fray.

And that should indeed scare the rest of the league.

With the 2026 college football season starting, 247Sports finalized its team-talent rankings , and the Florida Gators sit at No. 12 in the nation.

The No. 12 ranking is based on Florida's team-talent score of 859.91 using the site's standalone rankings. When sorting by the 247Sports Composite, which also factors in ESPN and Rivals rankings, Florida finds itself at No. 10 with a score of 891.07. Using both systems, Florida ranks Nos. 7 and 6, respectively, in the SEC. Georgia, Alabama, Texas, Texas A&M, LSU and Tennessee are ahead.

Considering the massive amount of roster turnover after Jon Sumrall took over the program, it's a testament to the quality of players brought in. There are nearly 60 new players on Florida's roster, including 32 transfers.

Key retentions by the new staff, such as running back Jadan Baugh, receivers Vernell Brown III and Dallas Wilson, linebacker Myles Graham, edge rusher Jayden Woods and cornerback Ben Hanks III, helped keep Florida's depth chart loaded with talent.

Talent doesn't always equal wins, though. Florida also ranked No. 12 a year ago, but the Gators finished the season 4-8. Injuries, scheme and luck all play a factor in whether a program gets the most out of its roster.

Florida has a challenging road ahead, including a nine-game SEC schedule. The talent is elite across the conference, with 13 teams inside the top 20 of these rankings. The Gators will not have an overwhelming edge against most of their opponents this season, but Sumrall has enough raw talent to make a quick turnaround realistic.

articles.title: Here’s how the Packers’ initial roster compares to previous years
articles.summary: Brian Gutekunst has been putting together rosters for most of a decade now. Here’s how it compares to previous seasons.
articles.body:
There are only so many ways you can stack a 53 man roster.

Despite plenty of handwringing year in and year out from fans and media alike as to what the roster will look like, the Packers' initial roster every year is configured in more or less the same way.

The same way, that is, with a couple of year-to-year fluctuations. Here's a quick look at where the Packers' 2026 initial roster differs and aligns with previous years.

At quarterback, the Packers kept just two players, the sixth consecutive year they've gone with two to start. The Packers last kept three quarterbacks on the roster in 2020, when Jordan Love was a healthy scratch for his entire rookie campaign.

It's a similar story at running back, where the Packers start with three for the fourth year in a row. They've kept three backs to start the season in five of the nine years of the Brian Gutekunst era.

Wide receiver is also on its own four-year streak. The Packers start the season with six wide receivers, the sixth time in nine years they've done that. They've kept more than six twice (eight in 2018 and seven in 2022) and fewer than six once (five in 2020).

Tight end is one of the most consistent positions across the entire Gutekunst era. They kept four this year and have kept four in seven of nine years under Brian Gutekunst. They've never gone higher than that, but have dipped down to three twice (in 2023 and 2024).

On the offensive line, the Packers kept 10 this year, one more than last year, but in line with larger recent trends; they've kept at least 10 in four of the last five years, jumping up to 11 in 2023.

Jumping up over to defense, the defensive line represents the biggest outlier on this year's roster. The Packers kept seven defensive linemen this year, the most they've ever carried to start the season.

Edge rusher is a different story. With Micah Parsons on the Physically Unable to Perform list, the Packers kept just four to start the season, just the second time in the Gutekunst era they've gone that light. The last time they kept four was 2019, when Za'Darius Smith and Preston Smith ended up soaking up a huge number of snaps ahead of a rookie Rashan Gary.

Off-ball linebacker is essentially in the same place as it was at the end of last season; swap Zaire Franklin for Quay Walker and you've told the tale. It's an increase over the start of last season, though; the Packers opened 2025 with just four linebackers on the roster.

Cornerback tends to have quite a bit of year-to-year fluctuation; the Packers haven't started the season with the same number of corners as the previous year since they kept six in both 2020 and 2021. They kept just five this year, though you could quibble with that number considering how much time Kamal Hadden has spent as a slot corner, a position often grouped with the safeties (look at Javon Bullard , for example). But the Packers call him a corner, so we kind of have to roll with that. Five corners it is, and it's pretty much in line with historical trends.

Hadden's inclusion as a corner means the Packers kept just four safeties, only the third time under Brian Gutekunst they've gone that low. But ever since they did their extreme makeover of the safety position in 2024, the position has been all but settled; Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard, and Kitan Oladapo make up the core of the group, and other than a few special teams cameos (we miss you, Zayne Anderson) there hasn't been much movement at safety since then.

Finally, the Packers kept three specialists. Surprised? You shouldn't be. They've never kept more than that (why would you, unless you drafted B.J. Sander and can't justify cutting him?), but have gone with fewer twice, floating through initial cuts with just two specialists in both 2021 and 2023, only to rectify the situation as soon as the waiver claim period resolved.

And that's the ultimate takeaway: the Packers' initial 53 man roster is just a snapshot, and the picture is going to change quickly. More than a few guys on this year's roster have won the worst prize in football: a spot on the initial roster that will quickly be taken away as the Packers handle waiver claims and other roster machinations as they trundle toward Week 1.

The process of making an NFL roster really never ends, but for now, this is what the roster looks like.

articles.title: 5 surprises (and explanations) from Broncos' initial 53-man roster
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos made a few surprising roster cuts this weekend. Here are the explanations for those decisions.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos made 38 roster moves this weekend to reach an initial 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season.

Going into their preseason finale, the Broncos only had one or two roster spots truly up for grabs, general manager George Paton explained in his post-cuts press conference on Sunday evening.

"Typically you look at the body of work," Paton said when asked how much the preseason finale influenced the final 53. "This is kind of the cherry on top, that last preseason game. We had a number of guys play well, whether it's Jordan Jackson or… I don't think it impacted a lot of these guys as it would in a lot of years. We were pretty set on where we were. We were probably at 55 or 54 before the last game, and maybe it just tweaked a little.

Denver fans were surprised by a few of Sunday's cuts, but there are explanations for all of them. Let's dive in.

1. Broncos cut FB Adam Prentice : It's a surprising cut because Prentice was a reliable fullback for Denver last season, and he just scored two touchdowns in preseason. There's a simple explanation, though. As a vested veteran, Prentice will not hit the NFL's waiver wire, so the Broncos are not risking losing him to another club. Prentice is expected to be signed to the practice squad , and his 2026 salary will not be guaranteed if he's not on the Week 1 active roster. Denver can elevate Prentice to the game-day roster up to three times from the practice squad, and he's expected to eventually be fully promoted to the active roster.

2. Broncos cut RB Jaleel McLaughlin : Denver ended up carrying four running backs, but McLaughlin did not make it, losing out to Tyler Badie for the RB4 job. Perhaps it shouldn't be a surprise after Badie previously beat out McLaughlin for RB3 duties last summer. McLaughlin is arguably a more talented runner, but Badie plays important roles on special teams, and he is a skilled pass blocker. "]W]ithout getting into details, it was a really hard decision," Paton said. "Obviously, special teams are involved, third-down ability. There's a lot involved, but that was probably the last decision we made, this fourth runner."

3. Broncos cut TE Justin Joly : The fifth-round draft pick struggled to make an impact during preseason (until a busted coverage allowed an 88-yard touchdown in the preseason finale). Had he been a seventh-round pick or undrafted free agent, Joly being cut wouldn't have been a surprise based on his performance. But we assumed his draft position made him safe. Denver's roster is too deep for Paton to think that way. "We knew he was raw," Paton said. "We still like the player. He was coming on towards the end of training camp. Tight end position is a tough position for a rookie. He missed a lot of the offseason, just a little bit behind. We wish we had another game or two. We still like the player. We think he's going to have a nice career. You just have to make tough decisions to build the best 53 you can make." The Broncos, of course, will try to re-sign Joly to the practice squad if he clears waivers.

4. Broncos cut LB Red Murdock : "Mr. Irrelevant" flashed in preseason, racking up tackles, but Denver opted to go with Karene Reid and Jordan Turner as the backup inside linebackers. Murdock, like Joly, will be a priority practice squad target if he clears waivers later today.

5. Broncos cut both of their long snappers : Denver cut incumbent starter Mitchell Fraboni and undrafted rookie Luke Basso. Fraboni is a vested veteran, so he won't have to clear the NFL's waiver wire. That will allow the Broncos to re-sign him to the practice squad, and Fraboni can be elevated to the game-day roster up to three times. Eventually, Fraboni will be fully promoted to the active roster, but beginning the season on the practice squad gives Denver more flexibility. The Broncos did the same thing with Prentice.

After waiver claims are processed, NFL teams can begin building their practice squads. Denver will build a 17-player practice squad , and they already have an international pass rusher lined up among their early signings.

articles.title: Las Vegas Raiders Cut Day: 4 Biggest Surprises
articles.summary: Cian Slone was unable to make it past the roster fringe despite impactful preseason play from Week 1 through Week 3.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders made it through cut day with an initial 53-man roster that makes sense. Nearly, 1200 men are losing out on either achieving their dream or proving to themselves that they can still hack it in this league. Once again, the Raiders made quality personnel moves and limited the head-scratcher to just a depth chart casualty.

Cian Slone being cut was probably the most questionable move of cut day. Slone has been phenomenal in every opportunity he has been given. As a playmaker, a pass rusher, a stunter, a tackler and a hustler. Nearly everyone who had eyes expected his play to be enough for him to force his way onto a team in need of pass-rushing playmakers.

A move that became even more eyebrow-raising when it was later revealed that Slone was cut despite third-round draft pick Keyron Crawford going on the season-ending Injured Reserve list. However, Slone is going to the waiver wire due to his lack of four years' tenure. The waiver wire order mirrors the draft order, so the Raiders are more likely than not to put him on the practice squad. Why? Because they are only keeping four edges on the roster.

Spytek has been a busy man this offseason, laying the foundation for future successes. What he isn't getting enough attention or credit for is the tenacity he has shown in finding ways to secure value out of cutting bait. Spytek has found teams to trade for players the entire world knows he was getting rid of.

Trading Jordan Meredith, last season's starting center and career backup guard, plus a 2029 seventh-round pick, for a 2027 sixth-round pick was a genius way to avoid outright cutting him. Meredith has struggled mightily at center, so much so that he was moved back to guard for the last preseason game and then moved on from.

Spytek's process may be a bit too methodical for many impatient fans in Raider Nation, but he's doing it the right way, cutting bait, making trades and adding talent where needed. Meanwhile, he has opted to draft premium skill positions rather than overpay in free agency, thereby allowing the coaching staff to keep most of his draft picks.

Keyron Crawford was the last Raider draft pick before the remaining prominent wide receivers were selected. Hindsight is always 20/20, but Jakobi Lane, Ted Hurst and Malachi Fields have all been lights out through training camp. Crawford getting injured in a preseason game and missing his rookie season is something no one wanted to see.

His not being designated for return is a horrible outcome, especially for a player who was blessed with extremely raw talent. His all-gas-and-no-brakes style displayed encouraging potential, but in order to learn how to hone it and use it without waste requires him to be on the field.

Is Atonio Mafi keeping a roster spot warm

Atonio Mafi hasn't pass protected well at all this preseason. In fact, one could say he's been a major contributing factor to the pass rush pressures that Fernando Mendoza faced on the second team. Nonetheless, he is still here because something about his run blocking overrules the fact that he is feeding sacks and pressures to defensive linemen.

Mafi is still practice squad eligible, so him making the 53-man roster implies that he is there for some purpose. Be it as depth or the first option to cut and send to the practice squad should Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak feel the need to add a player.

articles.title: Brewers, Cubs set for pivotal four-game series as September begins
articles.summary: LA CROSSE, Wis. (WLAX/ WEUX) – The Milwaukee Brewers and Chicago Cubs are set for a crucial four-game series at Wrigley Field as the calendar turns to Septem...
articles.body:
LA CROSSE, Wis. (WLAX/ WEUX) - The Milwaukee Brewers and Chicago Cubs are set for a crucial four-game series at Wrigley Field as the calendar turns to September.

Milwaukee enters the series with an eight-game lead over Chicago in the National League Central. The Brewers are 85-52 on the season, while the Cubs sit at 77-60.

The four games in Chicago are the first of seven straight meetings between the division rivals. After the series at Wrigley Field, the teams will meet for three more games in Milwaukee from September 7 through September 9.

Milwaukee currently leads the season series 4-2. However, Chicago won the last series between the teams in June, giving the Cubs some momentum heading into this matchup.

The timing of the series adds even more importance. With September baseball underway, the Brewers are looking to protect their position at the top of the division and continue their push toward the postseason. Milwaukee also enters the series with the best record in baseball.

The Cubs, meanwhile, are trying to close the gap. Chicago is coming off a 7-5 loss to the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday and has gone 2-4 over its last six games. Pete Crow-Armstrong provided much of the offense in Sunday's loss, hitting two home runs to bring his season total to 38.

Milwaukee has also been getting strong production from its young core. Jackson Chourio enters the series after a big week at the plate, hitting three home runs and reaching 20 for the season.

With seven head-to-head games coming over the next 10 days, this could be one of the most important stretches of the season for both teams.

The four-game series at Wrigley Field runs Monday through Thursday before the teams meet again next week at American Family Field.

articles.title: Liverpool complete £106m Bradley Barcola signing from PSG
articles.summary: Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth an initial £106million (€125m), ending their long pursuit of...
articles.body:
Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain in a deal worth an initial £106million (€125m), ending their long pursuit of the France international.

The agreement includes up to another £17m (€20m) in add-ons, while Liverpool have also made a £4.3m (€5m) solidarity payment connected to Lyon's sell-on entitlement from Barcola's 2023 move to PSG.

Barcola has signed a five-year contract at Anfield and will wear the No.29 shirt as he begins the next stage of his career in the Premier League.

"It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool," Barcola said after completing his move. "When I knew about Liverpool's interest in me, I didn't ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me."

The 23-year-old becomes Liverpool's third-most expensive signing after Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who both arrived in record-breaking deals last summer.

Barcola also follows Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet in joining permanently this summer, while Ronald Araujo has arrived on loan.

Liverpool identified another winger as a priority following Mohamed Salah's departure at the end of last season, with Barcola emerging as their leading target despite PSG initially placing a significantly higher valuation on him.

The negotiations stretched deep into August, with Liverpool also exploring moves for Brighton & Hove Albion winger Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr while attempting to reach an agreement with the French champions.

Barcola arrives after recording 13 goals and seven assists in 49 appearances for PSG last season, although Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue were regularly preferred in Luis Enrique's attack.

His prospects of remaining in Paris appeared increasingly uncertain after he was an unused substitute in the European Super Cup and then missed PSG's opening three domestic matchday squads.

The Lyon academy graduate also enhanced his reputation with France at this summer's World Cup, scoring three times while appearing in all eight of their matches.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola now gains a quick, direct forward capable of operating across the frontline as he continues reshaping the attack following Salah's departure.

Barcola already has experience of Anfield from his time with PSG and made clear that the atmosphere was part of the attraction of joining Liverpool.

His arrival provides the major attacking addition Liverpool have pursued throughout the summer and adds another proven option to a squad expected to challenge for the Premier League title.

After weeks of negotiations with PSG, Liverpool have finally secured the winger they identified as a central part of their plans for the post-Salah era.

Liverpool have confirmed that the 23-year-old will wear the number 29 shirt, as he did at Paris Saint-Germain. Barcola's decision to wear number 29 comes despite the availability of 11, which was recently vacated by Mohamed Salah.

Other shirts free in Andoni Iraola's squad include 16 and 17, though Barcola has chosen to continue with 29 for an unusual reason.

An odd shirt number choice for a marquee forward, Barcola has previously explained his affection for the shirt came via his love of FIFA, now known as EA Sports FC. The video game's 'The Journey' mode told the story of fictional character Alex Hunter , who wore 29.

"When I was younger, I used to play FIFA. In the story mode with Alex Hunter, this number became symbolic for me," Barcola previously explained.

"I thought to myself: 'The day I go pro, it'll be number 29.' And here I am, I adopted it, and now I'll never let it go."

articles.title: Duleep Trophy 2026-27 semi-final roundup: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, Tilak Varma hits century as Central Zone and South Zone lead at stumps on Day  2
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi continues to grip the audiences as he breaks yet another record by becoming the youngest player to score a Duleep Trophy 50.
articles.body:
15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest batter to score a Duleep Trophy half-century.

South Zone skipper Tilak Varma anchored his side's command in the parallel semi-final with a measured century.

Central Zone closed Day 2 at 45 for 3 in their second innings after both teams finished dead level at 266 runs.

Duleep Trophy 2026-27 semi-final roundup: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Tilak Varma shine on Day 2

Multi-day cricket rarely moves at the speed witnessed in Bengaluru on Day 2 of the Duleep Trophy semi-finals, but Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's breathtaking innings ensured the contest was anything but traditional. At just 15, the East Zone opener stuck a masterful fifty to put his side in a comfortable position.

While it didn't last long, the Central Zone's bowling attack caused an afternoon collapse that quickly reset the balance; Sooryavanshi proved his critics wrong. Despite coming to bat with a mediocre batting average of 16.53, his innings laid the groundwork for what allowed the side to match the defending champions' total.

Meanwhile, in the other semifinal showdown, South Zone skipper Tilak Varma scored an unbeaten century to show what it means to play with composure. His innings provided a textbook lesson in pacing a long-format knock while lower-order wickets tumbled around him.

At stumps, the tie between East Zone and Central Zone hung on a razor's edge. Central Zone reached 45 for 3 in their second innings, holding an effective 45-run lead after both teams ended their first innings level on 266, setting up a two-day shootout for a place in the final.

How Sooryavanshi's assault gave way to an East Zone collapse

Sooryavanshi's knock was less an innings and more a statement of intent. Opening alongside Abhimanyu Easwaran, the teenager reached his fifty off just 42 deliveries, punishing anything short or wide with five fours and three sixes.

Their opening stand reached 150 in just 146 balls, putting Central Zone's attack under severe strain early in the opening session. But Sooryavanshi eventually fell eight runs short of a maiden Duleep Trophy century, departing for 92 off 81 balls.

Despite missing out on three figures, his milestone surpassed Laxman Singh's 1969 record, making him the youngest player in the tournament's 65-year history to register a half-century. That initial foundation, however, was quickly squandered.

From 183 for 2 at lunch, East Zone lost their remaining eight wickets for just 83 runs. Central Zone's attack rallied through the middle overs, capitalising on a flurry of poor decisions and mid-match disruptions. to bowl the East Zone out for 266 in 57 overs, matching their own 1st innings total.

But while the East Zone stumbled after their explosive start, Tilak Varma provided a masterclass in what success in first-class cricket requires. From losing 5 wickets within 80 runs to a 175-run partnership with Shreyas Gopal for the sixth wicket, Varma totally changed the flow of the game.

On the other hand, the defending champs' second turn with the bat proved to be just as disappointing as the first, with the side losing their first three wickets within just 37 runs.

Why East Zone's middle-order failure hands the initiative back

Sooryavanshi's half-century will draw the headlines, and rightly so for a 15-year-old performing at this level. But scoring at better than a run a ball in a multi-day fixture carries limited weight if the rest of the batting lineup fails to capitalise on the foundation.

By failing to build a lead after a 150-run opening stand, East Zone handed momentum back to a Central Zone side that looked out of options before lunch.

With Central effectively 45 for 3, the remaining two days will depend entirely on whether East Zone's seamers can exploit a surface already showing signs of variable bounce.

Meanwhile, Varma is all set to add as many runs to the scoreboard before handing the batting back to the North Zone. His side already carried a comfortable 90-run lead. If he can push that into the triple figures, South Zone might be looking at a final berth.

articles.title: Jeepers Keepers: Liverpool’s Giorgi Mamardashvili and Lucca Brughmans
articles.summary: roll up roll up the circus finale is about to commence
articles.body:
It looks like there are more transfer moves being made by Richard Hughes before he jets off to be the new sporting director for Al Hilal and these two particular players weren't on this writer's summer transfer bingo card.

As was hoped, after a somewhat confusing and frustrating summer for transfers, there appears to be a furry of deals being reported that feel a lot more substantial than mere rumors. One particular position I don't feel any supporters were considering is goalkeeper yet according to various outlets there could be movement both ways with Nottingham Forest showing interest in Liverpool's current number two Giorgio Mamardashvili and 18 year-old Dutch keeper Lucca Brughmans replacing him.

It appears that Brughmans is having his medical now with parent club KRC Genk in agreement before a deal is finalized as the window is soon to be shut. The fee that's been circulated is close to £30M for the 6' 7" teenager and even though his senior appearances are only twelve games Brughman is being touted as a generational talent. It is also being reported that Genk will keep Braughmans for the rest of the season and join Liverpool next summer but with other rumors surfacing in regards Giorgi there could be a case where the Belgium teenager will find himself Liverpool's new number two keeper behind Alisson Becker.

The flip side to this news is the chance that Giorgi could be loaned out or even sold but as of yet this writer hasn't seen anything beyond Notting Forest approaching Liverpool about whether a deal is possible. This writer hopes that we hold onto our number two keeper this season because we all know that Alisson Becker always misses chunks of each season due to injuries and the trend has lengthened in time spent in recovery as Alisson ages.

Giorgi's career really took off when he joined Spanish club Valencia permanently, following a year loan, in December 2021 and during his time there he went 560 minutes consecutively without conceding a goal. In 2023 Giorgi was named Valencia's player of the year and continued to produce great numbers with his performances which attracted the attention of Liverpool who signed our present number two keeper in August 2024 and joined the summer before the 25/26 Premier League season. The promise was strong as a superb shot stopper and Giorgi had proved he rarely got injured which is a major factor for a team's consistency and so it looked like a clever move to ease the transition from one aging world class keeper to another upcoming one.

We've seen it before where a player is brought in with high hopes for player, club and supporters yet time on the bench, loan moves or other circumstances lead to the player's Liverpool career never really taking off and that could be what happens for Georgian keeper Giorgi Mamardashvili. This writer tends to look at a player's positives than judging negatively yet it's true that the biggest issue with supporters is Giorgi's inadequate distribution and ball-at-feet skills which could also be an issue with head coach Andoni Iraola.

Giorgi hasn't exactly won over the confidence amongst supporters and if these reports are true then it's not just the supporters who feel he isn't up to the task as Liverpool's number one when Alisson leaves (his contract is up next summer). Even so it does not seem wise to weaken our depth further than Hughes has already managed but the feelings about how our transfers have been handled since Jurgen Klopp left is more Wrecking ball than smart Moneyball or whatever the approach FSG and Hughes call it nowadays.

So this really could be a frantic and head scratching end to the summer circus of transfer dealings where more money will exchange hands, players will change clubs and one particular sporting director will be doing the same (there will be no good luck cards from the supporters Richard).

articles.title: Newcastle agree deal to sign Matias Fernandez-Pardo
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle is at St James’ Park. Newcastle United have reached an agreement to sign Belgian international forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from LOSC Lill...
articles.body:
Matthias Jaissle is at St James' Park. Newcastle United have reached an agreement to sign Belgian international forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from LOSC Lille, according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano.

The Magpies will pay a guaranteed €60 million plus add-ons to the Ligue 1 club after making a breakthrough in negotiations. Fernandez-Pardo has agreed personal terms and given the green light to the move. With paperwork finalised between the clubs, the 21-year-old is set to fly to England today for a medical and to sign his contract at St James' Park.

This high-profile signing is a major statement of intent from Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who was targeting a top attacking addition before the transfer deadline. After facing strong competition from European rivals including Liverpool and RB Leipzig, Newcastle moved decisively to meet Lille's valuation and secure one of Ligue 1's brightest young prospects.

Fernandez-Pardo's arrival addresses a key need in Newcastle's attack after significant squad changes earlier in the window. Comfortable as a winger on either flank or as a central forward, the Belgian brings explosive pace and one-on-one dribbling ability to Jaissle's side. Since joining Lille from KAA Gent, he has made his mark as a dynamic goal threat, recording 15 goal contributions across all competitions last season to help Lille secure Champions League qualification.

For Lille, the €60 million fee represents a significant financial windfall. The French club agreed to Fernandez-Pardo's departure after signing Japanese international Ayase Ueda from Feyenoord over the weekend as his replacement.

Barring any complications in his medical, Fernandez-Pardo will become Newcastle's marquee attacking signing of the summer window.

Fernandez-Pardo is expected to make his debut in Saturday's league match against Bournemouth, as Newcastle aim for a third consecutive win in all competitions.

It's almost impossible to look around the waiver wire and veteran releases from all 31 clubs and find targets; there were over 1,000 players released between Friday and Sunday, when the deadling to get down to 53 players expired.
